events.name: Drinking Chocolate With Prophecy Chocolate
events.description:
It is 2 pm on a Tuesday at Fabrik and you could use a pick me up while you get your work done. Luckily for all of us, Mateo of Prophecy chocolate will be coming down from Vermont to take care of you. He will make you a cup of chocolate and show you how to make a good one too. The chocolate drinking will only be about 30 minutes, but feel free to hang around, ask questions and chat. This is your chance to get a little nurturing and some great chocolate in the middle of the workday. Tuesday just got so much better.

AND....that is not all. We have a special guest straight from Oaxaca. His sister-in-law owns Sobre Masa in Brooklyn, a well respected restaurant featuring Oaxacan cuisine.

Gregorio is a master weaver and is a member of the only family in the region that is still fermenting a cousin of cacao called Theobroma Bicolor. It’s RARE and helps to create the beloved froth on some chocolate drinks. This is an extremely rare opportunity. Gregorio is also a master weaver who makes natural dyes. If you have ever wanted to visit Oaxaca, this is the closest you will get to it on a workday.

This is a free event for FABRIK MEMBERS.

Who are we?

Mateo is the founder of Prophecy Chocolate in Vermont. Mateo has spent years living in Peru, Colombia, and Mexico, learning directly from campesinos how cacao is grown, harvested, and transformed. In 2014, while living in the “Eyebrow of the Jungle” in Peru, he learned to make drinking chocolate using traditional methods, an experience that shaped his lifelong love for cacao.

He later imported heirloom cacao from the Cusco jungle and apprenticed in European‑style chocolate making. In 2019 he founded Prophecy Chocolate, creating craft chocolate from direct‑trade cacao. In 2025 and 2026, Prophecy Chocolate earned 13 medals in the International Chocolate Awards.

Mateo teaches about cacao at expos and universities, and when he isn’t making chocolate, he’s often on farms or in the forest, learning from growers and enjoying the plants that inspire his work

Nettie is the founder of The Chocolate Connection.

I create guided chocolate experiences that combine storytelling, history, sensory exploration, and first-hand stories gathered through years of traveling to cacao farms, meeting growers and chocolate makers, and exploring chocolate traditions around the world.

Chocolate is simply the starting point.

Through shared tasting, conversation, and immersive storytelling, guests gain a deeper appreciation for the people, cultures, and craftsmanship behind chocolate while creating meaningful connections with one another.

Every experience is designed to leave people feeling more present, more connected, and inspired to keep exploring long after the experience ends.

events.name: The Kalshi Crisis: Bets Over Baghdad
events.description:
Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN and CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there.

​So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch?

​For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders.

​For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, and worse actors. Polymarket and Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had.

​One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market.

​Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology and the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, and contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, and Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households and classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies.

​Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, and has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal and compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF and a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, and roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant.

​Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have.

​Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, and Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair and New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days and elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race and calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided.

​Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Sex, Crime, Gender: Hollywood and the Rise of Censorship
events.description:
A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.

Here's what you need to know!
We will begin with a short introduction and a film screening of the 1933 film Design for Living. After the screening, Matt Johnson will walk us through how the film is an insight into censorship.

Most people think of film history as a straight line — movies started out conservative and gradually pushed toward the sex and violence of today's blockbusters. That's not what happened.

Early Hollywood talkies were surprisingly bold. Frank depictions of sexuality, violence, and gender norms played out on screen at a moment of real cultural upheaval in America. It was freewheeling, daring, and genuinely revolutionary — until religious authorities, alarmed by what they called "filth" in America's mass media, began pushing back. Hard. The result was a self-imposed Hollywood Code that would reshape what American audiences were allowed to see for decades.

Sound familiar? America is currently in the middle of a strikingly similar cultural battle — book bans, library defunding, and political pressure on broadcasters are reshaping what people can access right now. Film historian Matt Johnson traces the arc from Pre-Code Hollywood to the rise of censorship — and makes the case that attempts to silence artistic output almost always produce something more subversive and more clever in return.
Matt Johnson teaches film theory and history at Franklin and Marshall College, where he is also a Fellow coordinating work in refugee resettlement and the question of welcome. He brings the same intellectual rigor and genuine curiosity to the history of Hollywood that he does to the most pressing questions of our time.

We'll explore:
* The surprisingly bold and daring films that existed before Hollywood self-censorship — and why they matter
* How religious, political, and cultural forces converged to impose the Hollywood Code
* Ernst Lubitsch and the "Lubitsch Touch" — how European filmmaking influenced and challenged Hollywood norms
* Why America has been here before — and what the history of censorship tells us about the cultural battles happening right now
* How artists have historically defeated censorship — and what that looks like today

Every dot is a real subway train. Eight hundred of them, give or take, form a small jazz combo (walking bass, piano, sax, vibes, brushes) that has been playing without pause for over a hundred years. On the platforms they are hot, screaming, full of complaint. This is the music inside the noise.  The harmony moves through a slow chorus. Whatever is playing now has not played before and will not play again.  Share your location and the trains nearest you grow louder. The piece rearranges itself around your body. You are listening to a portrait of where you stand, played by the city you are standing in.
Joshua Wolk is a designer and engineer who leverages data to make art.

* The music all around us in every day life.

events.description:
Expert-led lectures in bars and creative spaces across NYC.
 💭 Topic: "Freedom, Justice, and Democracy: History of the Reconstruction and Thaddeus Stevens" 🎤 Lecturer: Stephanie Townrow 📆 Date: Friday, September 9th ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Dumbo, Brooklyn
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
When the Civil War ended, the United States faced an enormous question: What kind of country would it become? Congressman Thaddeus Stevens believed the nation could not simply rebuild what had existed before the war. Instead, he called for radical changes to dismantle the South's old social and economic system, protect the rights of formerly enslaved people, and create a country built on a foundation of legal equality. This talk explores Stevens' bold vision for Reconstruction, the fierce opposition he faced, and why the questions he raised about freedom, justice, and democracy remain just as relevant today.

Stephanie Townrow is the Director of Interpretation and Exhibitions at the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy, a new museum she has had the privilege to build from the ground-up. A Ph.D. candidate in American history at the University of Delaware, she specializes in bringing the past to life through storytelling, artifacts, and the occasional deep dive down a historical rabbit hole. She has spent the last several years immersed in the world of Thaddeus Stevens and Lydia Hamilton Smith—and promises that Stevens was far more interesting (and important) than most history textbooks let on. She's excited to share some of the surprising stories behind one of America's most fascinating and fearless politicians.
We'll explore:
* The reconstruction of the United States post Civil War
* The radical changes that occured during this period which have led to the state of the country we live in today

What you’ll do

Attract and capture

Qualify

Book meetings

events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.
Official Website: UglyTalk.com

Founder Lab is a weekly build day for early-stage founders. Bring what you're stuck on — check in on what you're testing and what you learned, then get to work: office hours with investors and operators, and open build time with founders at your stage. Same day, every week.

​Who is this for?

​Founders building venture-scale startups, pre-seed to Series A — AI, deep tech, frontier, or any technical or science vertical. Connected through a common thread of relentless honesty and proof arc: something built to scale, tested and iterated on weekly.

​The System

​Every check-in runs through FounderOS, the proof engine that turns weekly work into a track record with venture visibility.

​Review Reps: How are you stuck, what did you learn, and what needs to change.

​Pressure-Test Logic: Use adversarial feedback to identify flaws in current hypotheses.

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

​Design the Next Interval: Lock the specific success gates for the upcoming build cycle.

​Direct Feedback: Receive "brutal honesty" testing from founders, operators, and venture advisors.

events.name: Building Slack's Simplified Layout Mode
events.description: This event will be online on YouTube & in-person (New York City). The speaker & live stream starts at 7:30 pm ET. In-person attendees may arrive as early as 7 pm ET. If arriving late, please leave a comment on this page & someone will come down ASAP. DescriptionSlack is a powerful hub for work & communication, but its dense & complex interface can be a barrier for users with motor, vision, & cognitive disabilities. To help more people use Slack effectively, we introduced Simplified Layout Mode on desktop & web. This preference transforms Slack into a single-column layout that is easier to navigate & has fewer distractions. In this session, we will demo Simplified Layout Mode & discuss its evolution from an accommodation request by an ALS advocacy group to a feature that benefits multiple audiences. Along the way, we'll share specific examples of how its design was shaped by our partnerships with disabled & neurodivergent users. Attendees will learn ... How to collect & synthesize feedback from different groups of users with disabilities over the course of a feature's developmentHow to collaborate with internal employee disability groups to get feedback & build momentum around a featurePresenter biosChris Xu is a director of product management of Slack looking after accessibility & design systems. Outside of product management, they have had a wide-ranging career focused on how technology & communities shape each other. They live in Brooklyn, NY & hold strong opinions about fruit. Lena Wang is a frontend software engineer at Slack working on accessibility & design systems. Outside of engineering, she's usually mid-side-quest - whether that's walking the entire length of Manhattan on a whim, running a Taco Bell 5k, or competing in a city-wide scavenger hunt. She lives in Manhattan, NY. Kaili Liang is a Software Engineer at Slack, working on accessibility & design systems. In her free time, she loves chasing new eats, diving into books, trying various arts & crafts, & traveling. AccessibilityThe presentation will have human captions [CC], not automatic captions. For ASL preferred speakers, learn about the Aira ASL App, & download it before the event. For the Blind & Low Vision community, learn about the Aira Explorer App & download it before the event. To access the online webinar for audio description, use the A11yNYC Access Offer to call, or simply inform your Visual Interpreter that you'd like that offer applied when you connect. For additional accessibility requirements, please email meryl@equalentry.com two weeks before the event. LivestreamYouTube Provided by Internet Society Accessibility SIG. Location detailsThe event is at 72 Spring street on the 4th floor. Everyone must be accompanied to the event on the 4th floor. Because everyone needs to be escorted, please arrive early or on time. When you enter the ground floor, a representative from A11yNYC will be there to provide elevator access. TransitThe building 72 Spring street is near several transit stops: 6 train Spring Street (non-accessible stop): 100 feetCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.4 milesB/D/F/M trains Broadway-Lafayette Street (accessible stop), 0.2 milesN/Q/R/W trains Prince Street (non-accessible stop): 0.2 milesCanal Street (accessible stop): 0.3 milesM1 / M55 Bus lines Broadway/Spring Street stop: 500 feetCabs & rideshares can let passengers out right near the building entrance. Finding the buildingIn Google Maps, find 72 Spring street. It shows the correct location of the entrance: on Spring Street, halfway between Crosby & Lafayette.It's also between the Glossier store & the Krewe Eyewear store.Inside & over the reception desk in our building 72 Spring st, it says Marc Jacobs. Traveling to the event?We recommend Hotel on Rivington or Crosby Street Hotel. AccreditationAll A11yNYC meetups are pre-approved for IAAP Continuing Accessibility Education Credits (CAEC). SponsorsThanks to Aira, AKQA, Deque, Evinced, Equal Entry, & Fable for sponsoring. Want to be a sponsor? Contact meryl@equalentry.com

events.name: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. About Farzad, the host Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C.   About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

NYC GTM Leaders, Vol. 1: Breaking Through the AI Slop Every channel is flooded with machine-generated outreach, & your buyers have stopped paying attention to any of it. So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. Now that everyone has shared context, conversations go deeper. 8:30 pm: Close & a first look at Vol. 2. Who should request an invite: GTM leaders at Series A+ startups Founders (Series A+, 2+ years in) Heads of Growth at scaling companies Seats are limited & approved individually. Request your invite now. Your hosts: Tanny Kang is Co-founder & COO at Vibranium Labs, an a16z-backed startup building AI-native incident management. A former Big Law tech attorney who traded redlines for pipeline, he now runs GTM end to end & has closed enterprise customers like Shutterstock, where Vibe OnCall cut manual incident work by 70% across 300+ engineers. He also writes Incidents.World, a newsletter on all things on-call. Josh Kim is Chief of Staff, GTM & Growth at Remy by MindStudio, an AI agent that builds enterprise-grade apps from a plain-language spec doc. A former Fortune 500 data & analytics consultant at Kantar, he's since helped drive 1.5x revenue growth & grown a community of 10,000+ builders, execs, & investors. Eric Fleshman is a GTM Engineer who has built go-to-market functions from the ground up, including founding GTME roles. His focus is what still breaks through when every inbox is machine-generated noise: technical depth, human-first outreach, & intent-driven systems. Signal first, intent after. He's an AlphaForge Architect Award winner from his Clay cohort & loves coffee, climbing & traveling! About Vibranium Labs: At vibraniumlabs.ai, we build Vibe OnCall, the #1 AI incident commander that proactively hunts down issues in your eng org before engineers ever get paged. We help engineering teams stay ahead of incidents, cut down on 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence. Our mission is straightforward: Prevent Incidents, Not Just Respond: Equip engineering orgs with an AI incident commander that proactively surfaces issues before they page anyone. Reduce On-Call Burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build Lasting Reliability: Offer ongoing tuning & partnership so Vibe OnCall keeps learning your systems & gets sharper the longer it runs.

Regroup at a bar nearby First Talk Description: Taming Dependency Graphs: Lessons from a 14-Year-Old iOS Codebaseby Victoria Ono As iOS apps grow over the years, managing dependencies becomes just as important as building new features. Understanding what depends on what, how new changes affect the codebase, & how to maintain architectural boundaries are challenges that every large engineering team eventually faces.In this talk, Victoria will share how Snapchat iOS codebase has evolved through the lens of their dependency injection frameworks. She'll cover what dependency graphs are, how they help reason about relationships across a large codebase, & how their approach to dependency injection has evolved to address the challenges that come with scale. Along the way, she'll talk about the architectural decisions behind that evolution & the lessons they have learned about managing complexity as applications grow. Victoria is an iOS engineer at Snap on the Maps team. Her recent work has focused on modernizing dependency injection within Maps & across the iOS codebase. Second Talk Description: The Soft Skills Nobody Taught Youby Mani Ramezan There's a lot of advice out there on how to prep for interviews & land your dream job. events.description: Join AssemblyAI & LiveKit for an evening with teams building voice agents on our stack-including Boardy, our co-host for the night. We'll kick things off with a live demo of Universal-3.5 Pro Realtime, AssemblyAI's newest Realtime speech-to-text model, now available on LiveKit Inference. We'll show how Context Carryover, conversation memory, multilingual support, & Voice Focus help voice agents built on LiveKit better understand users in real-world conversations. Then you'll hear from builders at Boardy & Flagler Health on what it actually takes to ship a voice agent that works in production. Before the event, you can choose to get a call from Boardy- a fully conversational AI matchmaker- to hear about who you are, why you're coming, & who you want to meet, then line up introductions with the right people. events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

events.name: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business To 7-Figures Without Raising Venture Capital
events.description: Everything I Learned Scaling My Business to 7-Figures Without Raising Venture CapitalI built Fibe to millions of dollars in profit without raising a dollar of venture capital, without a co-founder, & without a board. I still own the whole thing. Since then I've started The Shortlist, which has just begun to hit profitability, & cofounded Outliers Summit, which runs independently as a profitable events & media company that will cross seven figures soon. We run over a hundred events a year with a tiny team. On September 3 I'm walking through exactly how, in one session. What you'll leave with: How to pick the game you're playing before you start, so the advice you take actually applies to the business you're building Why one marketing channel is enough to reach a million dollars in revenue, & how to find yours How to build distribution before you have a product. I spent years building an audience before I had a business idea, & it is the single biggest reason bootstrapping worked How to find customers who will write a $50,000 check without blinking instead of ones who argue over $20 a month Then live Q&A for the rest of the session. Come with the specific question about your business, not the general one. That is where these earn their keep. Who this is for: anyone building something they would rather own outright than raise against. If you're going after a winner-take-all market & need capital to reach escape velocity, raising is the right call & this isn't for you.at. Mine wasn't.

events.name: From Concept To Conviction - AI In The Designer's Toolkit
events.description: Join us for an evening with Mareike Carolin Keller, Product Designer at Spotify, as she explores how to move AI from an experimental tool to a core part of your design workflow. Mareike will share how to leverage AI-assisted prototyping & code generation to accelerate execution & earn rapid stakeholder buy-in. As AI tools mature, the challenge for design teams is moving from informal experimentation to practical, daily utility. Mareike Carolin Keller will unpack how to embed AI directly into sprint cycles, validate complex ideas through real-time prototyping, & replace static mockups with interactive deliverables. Expect practical insights on using AI to bridge the gap between ideation & execution, ultimately driving faster cross-functional consensus. Mareike Carolin Keller (she/her) is a Product Designer at Spotify, where she focuses on creating cohesive, human-centered experiences across Spotify's growing multi-format platform. Her work spans across discovery & systemized distribution of content, as well as social experiences - helping millions of listeners seamlessly explore music, podcasts, & audiobooks. With a background in interaction design & experimental psychology, Mareike is passionate about crafting intuitive digital experiences that connect people to culture & creativity. Integrating AI into the design process transforms individual speed into team-wide capability. Mareike Carolin Keller shares how product designers can deploy AI tools in active production, build high-fidelity prototypes, & secure stakeholder alignment before committing heavy engineering resources. 01Evolving Design Workflows at Scale Learn how to establish clear frameworks that integrate AI capability directly into daily practice, transforming individual experimentation into institutional-grade capability. 02AI-Assisted Prototyping in Production Discover how to embed AI coding tools & custom generators directly into sprint cycles to validate complex ideas & test practical mechanics in real time. 03Accelerating Stakeholder Conviction Explore how to replace static mockups with high-fidelity, interactive prototypes that demonstrate actual product behavior, reduce decision friction, & secure immediate cross-functional buy-in.

events.name: New York Co-Founder Matching - Find a Partner by Solving Real Problems
events.description: Join a focused startup networking event in New York designed to help founders, builders and entrepreneurs meet potential co-founders through structured conversations and real business challenges. Instead of random networking and exchanging LinkedIn profiles, the evening focuses on meaningful conversations around startup ideas, skills, challenges and what participants are looking to build. What to Expect Co-Founder MatchingMeet people with complementary skills, backgrounds and ambitions through structured networking and guided conversations. Real Problem SolvingBring a real startup, business or product challenge and exchange ideas with other founders and builders who may offer a different perspective. Founder IntroductionsIntroduce yourself, share what you're building or looking to build, and explain what you are looking for in a potential co-founder. Targeted NetworkingConnect with entrepreneurs, developers, designers, marketers, operators and other professionals interested in building startups. Community MixerContinue conversations after the structured sessions and explore potential collaborations, partnerships and future startup opportunities. Who Should AttendStartup founders looking for a co-founderEntrepreneurs with an early-stage business ideaDevelopers and engineers looking for a business or product partnerDesigners, product managers and operators interested in founding a companySales, marketing and growth professionals looking to join a founding teamProfessionals interested in launching a startupAspiring entrepreneurs looking to meet complementary talent You don't need to have a fully developed startup to attend. events.name: The Builders Table
events.description: The Builder's Table is a weekly meetup for building out ideas with AI agents. Every month follows a rhythm. Every meeting has a focus. Must bring a laptop! Week 1 - Ideation & collaboration We'll have 1.5 hours to talk to one another, exchange ideas, ask questions, & refine what you'll be working on for the rest of the month. In the final 30 minutes, we'll start up our agents & have them create a step-by-step plan for building out your idea. Weeks 2 & 3 - Vibecoding Both meetups will be 2 full hours of straight vibecoding your project alongside everyone else. The idea is to take the plan you made at the end of week one & start building it out. Week 4 - Demo day The goal by the end of the month is to have a working project you can demo. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be polished or anywhere near perfect. As long as you have the bare bones of your idea & can show how it works, that's all that matters. We're focused on shipping, not perfection.   -Arrive at 4:45 -This meetup is intended for anyone looking to make more time for vibecoding. No need to commit to all the meetings in order to get something out of it. The intent is to form a community that is constantly building together. So you get out what you want to put in. Meetings will happen every week of every month, so we invite you to join us for food, drinks, good vibes, & vibecoding.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: WorkOS & You.com Agenda 5:30 pm - 5:35 pmWelcome & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  5:35 pm - 5:50 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  5:50 pm - 6:05 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from WorkOS TBA Outline:TBA  6:05 pm - 6:20 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker from You.com TBA Outline:TBA  6:20 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:30 pm - 6:40 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:40 pm - 6:50 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:50 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. events.name: Leaders In Fintech - Evolution Of Agentic Commerce
events.description: Join leading AI & product executives as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. Drawing on experience scaling complex transactional infrastructure, the panel will unpack practical models for deploying autonomous agents, securing machine-to-machine payments, & capturing enterprise value in agent-driven markets. Andr Kerr is the Director, Applied AI Lab at American Express, leading the strategy & execution of AI-driven product development. With a strong engineering background, he focuses on integrating generative AI technologies to enhance customer experiences & drive innovation within the financial services sector. Sailaja is a Director, Product Management - Agent Pay at Mastercard, where she launches innovative payment products across North America. She partners with major tech platforms & issuers to scale tokenized solutions that secure & simplify transactions, & brings 10+ years of experience across fintech, banking, & regulation driving innovation in complex, highly regulated environments. Join our panel of fintech leaders as they share frameworks for navigating the shift toward agentic commerce. They will unpack practical models for scaling autonomous execution across complex financial ecosystems while prioritizing security & customer trust. 01From Recommendations to Transactions Explore how AI systems are evolving from advisory roles to autonomous decision-makers capable of completing complex financial transactions. Learn how teams are designing products that seamlessly bridge conversational interactions with real-world execution. 02Trust, Security, & Payment Infrastructure Discover how leading institutions build secure, scalable payment rails designed specifically for autonomous agents. We'll examine how leaders manage risk, balance authorization with autonomy, & ensure ironclad trust across machine-driven financial interactions. 03The Machine-to-Machine Product Playbook Examine the strategies & frameworks product leaders use to build, launch, & scale machine-to-machine financial products. Learn how to adapt traditional product management playbooks to meet the demands of an increasingly agentic commerce ecosystem. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Settle in for easy conversation & good company in a warm, welcoming space. With a thoughtful selection of beer & wine on hand, it's the perfect backdrop for winding down or catching up.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.

events.name: Kubernetes Developers Meetup
events.description: Join the Elastic NYC User Group & Plural Kubernetes Developers on Tuesday, August 25th for an exciting meetup. We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? Email us at [meetups@elastic.co](mailto:meetups@elastic.co)Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food6:00 pm: Talk # 1 - Details coming soon - Michael Guarino (Plural)7:00 pm: Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic - Eric Mustin (Elastic)7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up Talk Details:Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic Eric Mustin (Elastic)Like Odysseus trying to find his way home, Kubernetes telemetry must navigate a difficult journey through dynamic workloads, short-lived infrastructure, overlapping tools, dropped signals, & unexpected operational monsters. This talk explores how Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic can work together to give Kubernetes metrics, logs, & traces a reliable path home. We'll look at practical collection architectures, Prometheus-native metrics, OpenTelemetry processing & routing, & how Elastic can bring the resulting signals together. Along the way, we'll discuss resiliency, duplication, architectural tradeoffs, & how to avoid getting lost at sea in an increasingly complex observability ecosystem.

events.name: The Builders Table
events.description: The Builder's Table is a weekly meetup for building out ideas with AI agents. Every month follows a rhythm. Every meeting has a focus. Must bring a laptop! Week 1 - Ideation & collaboration We'll have 1.5 hours to talk to one another, exchange ideas, ask questions, & refine what you'll be working on for the rest of the month. In the final 30 minutes, we'll start up our agents & have them create a step-by-step plan for building out your idea. Weeks 2 & 3 - Vibecoding Both meetups will be 2 full hours of straight vibecoding your project alongside everyone else. The idea is to take the plan you made at the end of week one & start building it out. Week 4 - Demo day The goal by the end of the month is to have a working project you can demo. Don't worry - it doesn't have to be polished or anywhere near perfect. As long as you have the bare bones of your idea & can show how it works, that's all that matters. We're focused on shipping, not perfection.   -Arrive at 4:45 -This meetup is intended for anyone looking to make more time for vibecoding. No need to commit to all the meetings in order to get something out of it. The intent is to form a community that is constantly building together. So you get out what you want to put in. Meetings will happen every week of every month, so we invite you to join us for food, drinks, good vibes, & vibecoding.

events.name: Strategic Forum
events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: Building Unified AI Workspace Across Enterprise Data
events.description: ODSC AI Skills Accelerator x Snowflake | New York City We meet at: 6:00 PM ET Location: Nomadworks, 240 West 40th Street, New York, NY 10018 Speaker: Joyce Avila, Chief Innovation Officer, DataWorthy.ai This event is part of the ODSC AI Skills Accelerator, bringing together AI & data professionals for practical sessions focused on real-world AI. Join ODSC AI & Snowflake in NYC to explore how Snowflake CoWork & CoCo can bring enterprise data together into a unified, no-code AI workspace. About the Session Organizations are rapidly enabling their teams to operational AI using governed data from multiple sources. However, most knowledge workers & business analysts can't afford the friction of protracted engineering projects or complex orchestration frameworks. This session demonstrates how Snowflake CowWork, powered by the no-code Snowflake CoCo experience, can become a unified "front door" to enterprise data spanning Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake Marketplace listings, native Snowflake tables, & staged unstructured files. We will walk through the design of a CoWork workspace that brings together customer profiles & engagement signals from Salesforce Data 360, third-party enrichment data from Marketplace, & internal fact tables in Snowflake, while also incorporating uploaded documents & other unstructured assets. Attendees will see how to declaratively describe data sources, define guardrails, & expose AI-driven workflows without writing traditional application code. By the end of the session, participants will have a concrete blueprint for delivering a no-code, agentic workspace where business users can ask complex questions, trigger guided actions, & collaborate on decisions across Salesforce Data 360, Marketplace data, internal Snowflake assets, & unstructured content. And, importantly, we'll learn how all of this can be achieved without sacrificing governance, performance, or architectural integrity. Come for the hands-on insights & stay to connect with NYC's AI & data community over complimentary food & drinks.  Space is limited, register to save your spot!

events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: Postgres Tuning In Age Of AI - Context Is Everything
events.description: Can AI tune a Postgres query? Give it only the SQL & you'll probably get some plausible-sounding advice. Give it the same context an experienced Postgres engineer would use, & things get much more interesting. In this talk, we'll first look at the Postgres performance, logging, & configuration data that's most useful for query tuning. We'll discuss why collecting the right information matters whether the consumer is a human or an AI, along with safeguards that help us use that information effectively & safely. Then we'll put it to the test. We'll work through a query performance problem by hand, examining the questions & evidence that guide the tuning process, before giving an AI access to that same environment through the pganalyze MCP server. Along the way, we'll explore how MCP can change the query tuning lifecycle, from finding the right problem to validating the fix, & which parts still require the same careful thinking they always have. Speaker:Ryan Booz Ryan is a Solutions Engineer at pganalyze focusing on PostgreSQL. Ryan has worked as a PostgreSQL advocate, developer, DBA & product manager for more than 25 years, primarily working with time-series data on PostgreSQL & the Microsoft Data Platform. Ryan is a long-time DBA & developer, starting with MySQL & Postgres in the late 90s. He spent more than 15 years working with SQL Server before returning to PostgreSQL full-time in 2018. He's at the top of his game when he's learning something new about the data platform or teaching others about the technology he loves.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households & classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies. Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, & has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal & compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF & a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, & roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant. Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have. Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, & Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair & New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days & elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race & calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided. Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

Mateo teaches about cacao at expos and universities, and when he isn’t making chocolate, he’s often on farms or in the forest, learning from growers and enjoying the plants that inspire his work

events.name: The Kalshi Crisis: Bets Over Baghdad
events.description:
Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN and CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there.

​So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch?

​For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders.

​For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, and worse actors. Polymarket and Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had.

​One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market.

​Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology and the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, and contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, and Fox News. Her entire career argues that being a citizen is something you practice, not something you trade: that civic life has to be built deliberately, in households and classrooms, not aggregated through the same mechanisms that price pork bellies.

​Yehuda Maes is a Harvard Law grad ('23), former Bain consultant, former Citadel Securities trader, and has run client engagement at Norm AI, anthe AI company building legal and compliance infrastructure for institutional finance. Before all of that he was a Sergeant in the IDF and a BlackRock analyst. He's spent his entire adult life inside the machinery that puts a price on sovereign debt, legal risk, and roughly everything else. He thinks that's a feature, not a bug. He's the perfect defendant.

​Two perspectives. One night. And probably a few people in the room with open positions they shouldn't admit they have.

​Moderated by Gillian Goodman, a Columbia Journalism School grad whose work has appeared in The Intercept, Truthout, Prism, and Democracy Now!, with features in Vanity Fair and New York Magazine. She covered the Columbia encampments from the first days and elections in coastal Georgia from inside the precincts. She knows the difference between calling a race and calling a price. Let's get it on. Drinks provided.

​Accessible. Engaging. Social. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Sex, Crime, Gender: Hollywood and the Rise of Censorship
events.description:
A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.

Here's what you need to know!
We will begin with a short introduction and a film screening of the 1933 film Design for Living. After the screening, Matt Johnson will walk us through how the film is an insight into censorship.

Most people think of film history as a straight line — movies started out conservative and gradually pushed toward the sex and violence of today's blockbusters. That's not what happened.

Early Hollywood talkies were surprisingly bold. Frank depictions of sexuality, violence, and gender norms played out on screen at a moment of real cultural upheaval in America. It was freewheeling, daring, and genuinely revolutionary — until religious authorities, alarmed by what they called "filth" in America's mass media, began pushing back. Hard. The result was a self-imposed Hollywood Code that would reshape what American audiences were allowed to see for decades.

Sound familiar? America is currently in the middle of a strikingly similar cultural battle — book bans, library defunding, and political pressure on broadcasters are reshaping what people can access right now. Film historian Matt Johnson traces the arc from Pre-Code Hollywood to the rise of censorship — and makes the case that attempts to silence artistic output almost always produce something more subversive and more clever in return.
Matt Johnson teaches film theory and history at Franklin and Marshall College, where he is also a Fellow coordinating work in refugee resettlement and the question of welcome. He brings the same intellectual rigor and genuine curiosity to the history of Hollywood that he does to the most pressing questions of our time.

We'll explore:
* The surprisingly bold and daring films that existed before Hollywood self-censorship — and why they matter
* How religious, political, and cultural forces converged to impose the Hollywood Code
* Ernst Lubitsch and the "Lubitsch Touch" — how European filmmaking influenced and challenged Hollywood norms
* Why America has been here before — and what the history of censorship tells us about the cultural battles happening right now
* How artists have historically defeated censorship — and what that looks like today

 💭 Topic: "Freedom, Justice, and Democracy: History of the Reconstruction and Thaddeus Stevens" 🎤 Lecturer: Stephanie Townrow 📆 Date: Friday, September 9th ⏰ Doors Open: 6:30 PM 📍 Location: Dumbo, Brooklyn
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
🤝 A little about us: Wisdom Bar is a social lecture series hosted in cool bars and creative spaces throughout New York City. Each event features a presentation from an expert speaker whose passion for a unique topic guides the room. We'll explore new ideas, exchange perspectives, and learn something new along the way, all in an effort to get curious-minded people together for drinks and thoughtful conversation. If this sounds like something you might enjoy, we'd love to host you.
Here's what to look forward to during this groundbreaking lecture:
When the Civil War ended, the United States faced an enormous question: What kind of country would it become? Congressman Thaddeus Stevens believed the nation could not simply rebuild what had existed before the war. Instead, he called for radical changes to dismantle the South's old social and economic system, protect the rights of formerly enslaved people, and create a country built on a foundation of legal equality. This talk explores Stevens' bold vision for Reconstruction, the fierce opposition he faced, and why the questions he raised about freedom, justice, and democracy remain just as relevant today.

Stephanie Townrow is the Director of Interpretation and Exhibitions at the Thaddeus Stevens & Lydia Hamilton Smith Center for History and Democracy, a new museum she has had the privilege to build from the ground-up. A Ph.D. candidate in American history at the University of Delaware, she specializes in bringing the past to life through storytelling, artifacts, and the occasional deep dive down a historical rabbit hole. She has spent the last several years immersed in the world of Thaddeus Stevens and Lydia Hamilton Smith—and promises that Stevens was far more interesting (and important) than most history textbooks let on. She's excited to share some of the surprising stories behind one of America's most fascinating and fearless politicians.
We'll explore:
* The reconstruction of the United States post Civil War
* The radical changes that occured during this period which have led to the state of the country we live in today
* The role that Thaddeus Stevens played in shaping our nation
This might be for you if you...
* Are curious about unknown figures in our shared history
* Are intrigued by the steps taken by the government during the Reconstruction era that have directly impacted where the US is today

Build the full path from a stranger to a booked meeting to a closed deal, and know exactly what it costs you.

What’s covered

Build the complete sales funnel, not just the top of it.

You’ll learn how to attract and capture leads, qualify them so you spend time on the right prospects, automatically book meetings, follow up without losing anyone, and measure what every stage costs.

What you’ll do

Attract and capture

Map the entire funnel with Claude, stage by stage.
Create a lead magnet that solves one urgent problem.
Build a landing page and opt-in form that captures the lead.

Qualify

Add qualifying questions covering budget, timeline, need, and decision-making authority.
Use Claude and your CRM’s lead scoring to automatically separate hot leads from cold ones.

Book meetings

Connect a scheduling tool so qualified leads can instantly book a call.
Add confirmations and reminders designed to reduce no-shows.

Follow up and close

Write a nurture sequence and automated follow-ups with Claude.
Include dedicated paths for no-shows and rescheduling.
Configure your CRM to draft a personalized follow-up after each meeting so no opportunity quietly evaporates.

Measure the money

Set up the numbers that determine whether the funnel is working, including cost per lead, cost per booked meeting, customer acquisition cost, and conversion rates between each stage.
Use Claude to interpret the dashboard, identify where money is leaking, and suggest what to fix first.

The proposal also highlights two longer-term metrics founders should watch: lifetime value compared with customer acquisition cost, and the time required to recover acquisition costs.

Recommended stack: Claude for copy, scoring logic, and interpreting performance; HubSpot’s free CRM for lead capture, scoring, pipeline management, and reporting; Calendly or Cal.com for scheduling; and Systeme.io as an all-in-one option for landing pages, email, and funnels.

Other tools considered: Chili Piper and RevenueHero for high-volume inbound teams, ClickFunnels for templates, GoHighLevel for agencies, and ActiveCampaign for advanced email automation.

You’ll leave with: A live funnel that captures, qualifies, books, and follows up with leads, plus a simple dashboard showing what each stage costs.

Programming note: The proposal identifies this as the most content-dense session and suggests that it may work better as two separate evenings, one focused on building and capturing leads, and another focused on qualification, booking, and measurement.

events.description:
A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.
