events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.description: Join us for the next AI Tinkerers meetup in NYC! Showcase your latest AI demos, connect with fellow practitioners, & dive deep into the world of LLMs & generative AI with the best technical community in NYC. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQSome slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? events.name: Claude Code Workshop
events.description: Learn to orchestrate AI agents that write & ship code for you. Claude Code is already changing how the best engineering teams ship. This workshop, presented with Provectus, is a chance to build with it directly - not watch a demo, not sit through slides about it. You'll leave having shipped something real, with a working sense of how to bring this back to your own team. We'll spend a little time on context - how Claude Code fits into modern engineering workflows & where teams are seeing the biggest wins. Then the slides go away, & you're at a build station with Anthropic engineers & Provectus partners beside you, orchestrating agents that write & ship code while you direct the work.   Why attend Ship real output. Your agents write the code - you direct them. You'll leave with something you actually built, not a slide deck about what's possible. See best practices in action. Learn how Claude Code fits into enterprise workflows, from the people who deploy it at scale. Get direct support. Live help at every table from Anthropic engineers & Provectus partners - no one gets stuck on an error alone. Build your network. Spend the afternoon with technical leaders wrestling with the same questions you are.   Who should attend Engineering Leaders - EMs, VPs, CTOs, Platform Leads, Principal Engineers Business Leaders - CPOs, Digital Transformation, senior AI sponsors, PMs You don't need to be an engineer. If you're making decisions about AI investment or setting strategy, understanding what Claude Code actually does is the edge.   Agenda 1:00 PM - 2:30 PM: Registration & setup support 2:30 PM - 3:00 PM: Welcome, Claude Code overview, demo 3:00 PM - 5:00 PM: Build session: hands-on with Claude Code 4 PM - 5 PM: Networking Happy Hour   What to bring Your laptop - Basic comfort with a terminal or code editor is helpful but not required - you'll be directing AI agents & building alongside them, & our team supports you the whole way.   The fine print The event is free to attend if selected. Registration is required & subject to approval. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis - apply early. Want to bring a colleague? Have them apply separately - every seat needs its own approved registration.

events.name: Tech Council Summit
events.description: 2026 is the year of enterprise AI deployment. The window for experimentation has closed; the time for ROI is fast approaching. At the WSJ Technology Council Summit, the world's leading enterprise technology executives will debate the accelerated journey from experimentation to value. Key themes include: Balancing CEO demand for rapid AI rollout against the need for modernization of legacy systems, employee adoption & enterprise-wide change managementHow technology leaders can control cost, value, productivity & ROI when the economics of AI are still evolvingMitigating the cybersecurity risks associated with the latest frontier models & operationalizing agentic defenseEvaluating build versus buy, centralized versus decentralized AI governance & striking a balance between horizontal & vertical AI deployment - all at a time when the enterprise software sector is facing significant disruptionReviewing the Trump administration's technology policies & debating their impact on enterprise technology leaders todayHow geopolitical uncertainty can increase the risk of cyber attacksHow technology leadership is evolving to drive business strategyThe summit is built with extensive input from WSJ Technology Council members, & will balance the timeliness & newsworthiness of WSJ live events with the relevance & exclusivity of our peer community. Expect news, peer discussions, real-time polling & unrivaled networking.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works:15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Situational Awareness. Are we in an AI bubble? Circular financing between AI labs & infrastructure players, record market concentration, & capex spending that's outpacing monetization. We're decoding the real risk signals versus the noise, & what it means for how you invest from here. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time. Disclaimer By registering for this event, you'll be added to the Innovest newsletter (innovest.substack.com). You can unsubscribe at any time.

events.description: In partnership with Citi, Finnair, Helsingin Kaupunki, PwC, Sullivan & Worcester & Team Kentucky. The FACC-NY Strategic Forum 2026 brings together leaders from business, technology, public policy, & innovation on both sides of the Atlantic. Held at a pivotal moment for global business & geopolitics, this year's forum explores how Finnish companies are building competitive advantage to succeed in the U.S. market in an increasingly complex global environment. We are honored to welcome keynote speaker James A. Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; Miia Rantanen, Consul General of Finland in New York; Helen Mets, President & CEO of Ahlstrom; Massimo Reynaudo, President & CEO of UPM-Kymmene Corporation; Susan Duinhoven, former President & CEO of Sanoma & Board Member of KONE, Kemira, & Fiskars Group; Sauli Sinisalo of Bluefors; Dr. Jan Goetz, CEO & Co-Founder of IQM Quantum Computers; Jussi-Pekka Penttinen, CEO, CTO, & Co-Founder of Vexlum; Ronit Ghose, Global Head of Future of Finance at Citi; & Juhani Sirn, Region Head for Trade Promotion, North America, Consulate General of Finland in New York, alongside senior executives, founders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders joining throughout the day. Program HighlightsBridging the Gap - How international CEOs translate Finnish innovation into U.S. & global market successLeadership Under Pressure - Perspectives from sports & business on resilience, performance, & decision-making in high-pressure environmentsNordic Quantum Edge - How Nordic companies are shaping the future of quantum technology, advanced computing, & deep tech innovationThe forum offers strategic discussions, forward-looking insights, & networking opportunities with leaders shaping the future of Finnish-American business relations. Attendance & MembershipFACC-NY members receive priority access to Strategic Forum 2026. Ticket allocations are included in FACC-NY membership tiers as follows: Platinum Members: 3 ticketsGold Members: 2 ticketsSilver & Bronze Members: 1 ticketIndividual Members: 1 ticketCompanies & individuals interested in attending are encouraged to become FACC-NY members to access the event & participate in our year-round network of executive programs, industry events, & business connections. Corporate memberships start at $1,000 & Individual memberships start at $250 (Young Professionals at $50). Read more about becoming a member & purchase your membership here: https://facc-ny.com/memberships/.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. events.name: Brains In Sync - Neuroscience Of Music, Drugs & Shared Experience
events.description: This is not a dry academic talk. Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. When a room full of strangers moves to the same beat, their brains start to move together too. This talk explores the neuroscience of interbrain synchrony, such as how music, rhythm, & altered states pull separate nervous systems into a shared rhythm, from ritual dance to the modern rave. We'll trace the math underneath the music (fractal structure, wave dynamics) up through the psychology of the dance floor, & into the clinic, where music is increasingly used as a deliberate tool in psychedelic-assisted therapy. Drawing on years inside the cannabis industry & hands-on psychedelic pharmacology research, this talk breaks down what's actually happening in the brain on psychoactive substances: shifts in perception, cognition, & the neurochemistry behind altered states, plus what's driving their growing clinical use in therapy.   Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. Agenda: Doors Open: 6:30 PM Lecture + Q&A: 6:45 PM - 8 PM Open-form networking: 8 PM & onwards Whether you're a parent, student, educator, or just someone fascinated by neuroscience, this is the perfect first night for PhDs & Pints. Smart people. Cold drinks. Big conversations.

Winnefeld Jr., former Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff & one of the United States' leading voices on strategy, leadership, & global security. Confirmed speakers also include Leena-Kaisa Mikkola, Ambassador of Finland to the United States at the Embassy of Finland in Washington; events.name: Agentics - Use Agents Effectively
events.description: Join Nori Agentic & Modal (featuring Warp, Opus, Goose, Librechat, & Subconscious) in New York on August 19 for our second flagship Agentics speaker series - a full evening of presentations from teams at the cutting edge of agentic development. Whether you're just getting started with AI coding agents (beginner friendly!) or you've been shipping with them for months, you'll walk away with practical techniques you can use the next day. Dinner will be provided! A recap of our last event: agenticsnyc.com/events/may-2026-speaker-series.html Huge thanks to our sponsors, MongoDB & Clickhouse! MongoDB is the leading modern database platform empowering developers to build flexible, scalable, data-driven applications. Check-out the MongoDB for Startups for Atlas credits & Voyage AI tokens, technical expertise, & dedicated support on the world's best modern, AI-ready data platform. ClickHouse is one of the fastest & most resource-efficient real-time databases & data warehouses, optimized for diverse data-intensive & large-scale workloads. Applications range from interactive & user-facing to ad-hoc historical analyses. Planned Schedule: 6 PM: Doors Open 6:30 PM - 9 PM: Presentations 9 PM - 10 PM: Networking Each presentation will be ~10 minutes with a ~5 minute Q&A, 7 presentations total. We don't expect to use the full 2.5 hours for presentations, but we're estimating conservatively. Speakers: Aloke Desai is the head of product engineering & first engineering hire at Warp. He's been building agents for 5 years at Warp, helping scale it to millions of active users. Prior to Warp, he was a senior engineer & tech lead at Google Docs. Aloke's talk will focus on how a software factory can self-improve over time. Amol Kapoor is the CEO of Nori, the lead organizer of Agentics, & the author of 12 Grams of Carbon. He's been in the AI world for 12 years, including a 4-year stint at Google Research. Nori uses background agents to do just about everything - an army of agents respond to errors, manage the CRM, keep data clean, & more. In his talk, Amol will walk through what a "software factory" is, how to build one, & what pitfalls to avoid. Danny Avila is the founder & core maintainer of LibreChat. He was early to recognize the need for cross-provider dev tools, & started LibreChat 3 years ago to create a chat UI experience separated from the big labs. Danny will be speaking about how LibreChat solved multiplayer agent/human sandboxes. Jack Amadeo is a software engineer on the Goose team at Block & one of the most prolific contributors to Goose, Block's open-source AI agent. He joined Block via the acquisition of Neptyne, the YC-backed Python spreadsheet startup he co-founded, & was previously an engineer at Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. His Goose work spans the multi-provider LLM architecture, MCP integration, & the Goose SDK. Jack will speak about unbundling the Goose harness into an SDK & the uses that emerge from treating agents as SDKs. Jack O'Brien is a two-time founder & ex-Googler, & the current CEO of subconscious.dev. LLMs are incredible tools with one massive limitation: the context window. They are fundamentally limited in what they can remember. Jack has spent the last two years thinking about how to make this problem better. He'll be speaking about context compression & long-horizon tasks in modern LLMs. Jeffrey Silver is the CTO & cofounder of Opus. Over the last 6 years, Jeff has spent a lot of time thinking about how to build tools that benefit everyone at Opus, including non-technical team members. That focus led him to build one of the first cloud agent stacks. Jeff will be speaking about how Opus uses their cloud agent army to manage their on-call burden. Qijia (Joy) Liu is an early Member of Technical Staff at Modal & a Penn M&T grad. She came up through Penn Labs before joining Modal, where she's focused on making serverless GPU infrastructure accessible to ML engineers. Joy will show you how to vibe train a model on Modal Training Gym, an RL library that lets users post-train on Modal in under 100 lines of code. Agentics is a community of 1000+ people building with coding agents. We meet in New York City to share what actually works, what doesn't, & what's next. We're reinventing best practices every day (without having to be glued to Twitter). Learn more here: https://agenticsnyc.com/ Sign up for the newsletter: https://noriagentic.com/newsletter.html#agentics And join our community slack: https://join.slack.com/t/nori-7sp2119/shared_invite/zt-3nvw8xlw2-hxppg~NXeawHVvopmbMCFw

Join Nori Agentic & Modal (featuring Warp, Opus, Goose, Librechat, & Subconscious) in New York on August 19 for our second flagship Agentics speaker series - a full evening of presentations from teams at the cutting edge of agentic development. Whether you're just getting started with AI coding agents (beginner friendly!) or you've been shipping with them for months, you'll walk away with practical techniques you can use the next day. Dinner will be provided! A recap of our last event: agenticsnyc.com/events/may-2026-speaker-series.html Huge thanks to our sponsors, MongoDB & Clickhouse! MongoDB is the leading modern database platform empowering developers to build flexible, scalable, data-driven applications. Check-out the MongoDB for Startups for Atlas credits & Voyage AI tokens, technical expertise, & dedicated support on the world's best modern, AI-ready data platform. ClickHouse is one of the fastest & most resource-efficient real-time databases & data warehouses, optimized for diverse data-intensive & large-scale workloads. Applications range from interactive & user-facing to ad-hoc historical analyses. Planned Schedule: 6 PM: Doors Open 6:30 PM - 9 PM: Presentations 9 PM - 10 PM: Networking Each presentation will be ~10 minutes with a ~5 minute Q&A, 7 presentations total. We don't expect to use the full 2.5 hours for presentations, but we're estimating conservatively. Speakers: Aloke Desai is the head of product engineering & first engineering hire at Warp. He's been building agents for 5 years at Warp, helping scale it to millions of active users. Prior to Warp, he was a senior engineer & tech lead at Google Docs. Aloke's talk will focus on how a software factory can self-improve over time. Amol Kapoor is the CEO of Nori, the lead organizer of Agentics, & the author of 12 Grams of Carbon. He's been in the AI world for 12 years, including a 4-year stint at Google Research. Nori uses background agents to do just about everything - an army of agents respond to errors, manage the CRM, keep data clean, & more. In his talk, Amol will walk through what a "software factory" is, how to build one, & what pitfalls to avoid. Danny Avila is the founder & core maintainer of LibreChat. He was early to recognize the need for cross-provider dev tools, & started LibreChat 3 years ago to create a chat UI experience separated from the big labs. Danny will be speaking about how LibreChat solved multiplayer agent/human sandboxes. Jack Amadeo is a software engineer on the Goose team at Block & one of the most prolific contributors to Goose, Block's open-source AI agent. He joined Block via the acquisition of Neptyne, the YC-backed Python spreadsheet startup he co-founded, & was previously an engineer at Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs. His Goose work spans the multi-provider LLM architecture, MCP integration, & the Goose SDK. Jack will speak about unbundling the Goose harness into an SDK & the uses that emerge from treating agents as SDKs. Jack O'Brien is a two-time founder & ex-Googler, & the current CEO of subconscious.dev. LLMs are incredible tools with one massive limitation: the context window. They are fundamentally limited in what they can remember. Jack has spent the last two years thinking about how to make this problem better. He'll be speaking about context compression & long-horizon tasks in modern LLMs. Jeffrey Silver is the CTO & cofounder of Opus. Over the last 6 years, Jeff has spent a lot of time thinking about how to build tools that benefit everyone at Opus, including non-technical team members. That focus led him to build one of the first cloud agent stacks. Jeff will be speaking about how Opus uses their cloud agent army to manage their on-call burden. Qijia (Joy) Liu is an early Member of Technical Staff at Modal & a Penn M&T grad. She came up through Penn Labs before joining Modal, where she's focused on making serverless GPU infrastructure accessible to ML engineers. Joy will show you how to vibe train a model on Modal Training Gym, an RL library that lets users post-train on Modal in under 100 lines of code. Agentics is a community of 1000+ people building with coding agents. We meet in New York City to share what actually works, what doesn't, & what's next. We're reinventing best practices every day (without having to be glued to Twitter). Learn more here: https://agenticsnyc.com/ Sign up for the newsletter: https://noriagentic.com/newsletter.html#agentics And join our community slack: https://join.slack.com/t/nori-7sp2119/shared_invite/zt-3nvw8xlw2-hxppg~NXeawHVvopmbMCFw

Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. The current cohort presents at Demo Day, open to the network. You can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. events.name: Tech x Market Decoders (This week's topic - Anthropic's IPO)
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. This week's topic: Anthropic's upcoming IPO Anthropic filed confidentially for one of the most anticipated debuts in years, with a listing expected in Sept/Oct 2026. We're decoding the business behind Claude; the revenue growth, the compute costs, & whether the valuation actually holds up once Wall Street gets a look. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What it can't do is connect the dots around a a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works:15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Situational Awareness. Are we in an AI bubble? Circular financing between AI labs & infrastructure players, record market concentration, & capex spending that's outpacing monetization. We're decoding the real risk signals versus the noise, & what it means for how you invest from here. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. About Us This event is organized by Innovest, a media-led intelligence platform at the intersection of tech & markets, built for operators, investors, & founders. Through newsletters, a growing library of business models, & events like this one, we're building the judgment, experience, & taste that no AI can replace - one pattern, one playbook, one signal at a time. Disclaimer By registering for this event, you'll be added to the Innovest newsletter (innovest.substack.com). You can unsubscribe at any time.

events.description: NYC GTM Leaders, Vol. 1: Breaking Through the AI Slop Every channel is flooded with machine-generated outreach, & your buyers have stopped paying attention to any of it. So what still breaks through? Join us Thursday, August 27th in Midtown (address shared upon approval) for an off-the-record evening with GTM leaders who are figuring it out in real time. Capped at 50 so the conversations stay focused & real. The agenda: 6:30 pm: Doors open. Drinks, light bites, & an icebreaker to get the room talking. 7:00 pm: GTM Insight Talks. Three quick-hit talks from operators actually running these plays: using AI for lead gen without sounding like AI, thought leadership as a channel buyers still trust, & a head-to-head teardown of real GTM stacks. Q&A after. 7:30 pm: Working session. Small groups, hands-on. Apply the plays to your own pipeline. 8:00 pm: Round two networking. Now that everyone has shared context, conversations go deeper. 8:30 pm: Close & a first look at Vol. 2. Who should request an invite: GTM leaders at Series A+ startups Founders (Series A+, 2+ years in) Heads of Growth at scaling companies Seats are limited & approved individually. Request your invite now. Your hosts: Tanny Kang is Co-founder & COO at Vibranium Labs, an a16z-backed startup building AI-native incident management. A former Big Law tech attorney who traded redlines for pipeline, he now runs GTM end to end & has closed enterprise customers like Shutterstock, where Vibe OnCall cut manual incident work by 70% across 300+ engineers. He also writes Incidents.World, a newsletter on all things on-call. Josh Kim is Chief of Staff, GTM & Growth at Remy by MindStudio, an AI agent that builds enterprise-grade apps from a plain-language spec doc. A former Fortune 500 data & analytics consultant at Kantar, he's since helped drive 1.5x revenue growth & grown a community of 10,000+ builders, execs, & investors. Eric Fleshman is a GTM Engineer who has built go-to-market functions from the ground up, including founding GTME roles. His focus is what still breaks through when every inbox is machine-generated noise: technical depth, human-first outreach, & intent-driven systems. Signal first, intent after. He's an AlphaForge Architect Award winner from his Clay cohort & loves coffee, climbing & traveling! About Vibranium Labs: At vibraniumlabs.ai, we build Vibe OnCall, the #1 AI incident commander that proactively hunts down issues in your eng org before engineers ever get paged. We help engineering teams stay ahead of incidents, cut down on 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence. Our mission is straightforward: Prevent Incidents, Not Just Respond: Equip engineering orgs with an AI incident commander that proactively surfaces issues before they page anyone. Reduce On-Call Burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build Lasting Reliability: Offer ongoing tuning & partnership so Vibe OnCall keeps learning your systems & gets sharper the longer it runs.

events.name: Brains In Sync - Neuroscience Of Music, Drugs & Shared Experience
events.description: This is not a dry academic talk. Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. When a room full of strangers moves to the same beat, their brains start to move together too. This talk explores the neuroscience of interbrain synchrony, such as how music, rhythm, & altered states pull separate nervous systems into a shared rhythm, from ritual dance to the modern rave. We'll trace the math underneath the music (fractal structure, wave dynamics) up through the psychology of the dance floor, & into the clinic, where music is increasingly used as a deliberate tool in psychedelic-assisted therapy. Drawing on years inside the cannabis industry & hands-on psychedelic pharmacology research, this talk breaks down what's actually happening in the brain on psychoactive substances: shifts in perception, cognition, & the neurochemistry behind altered states, plus what's driving their growing clinical use in therapy.   Expect storytelling, humor, surprising insights, & plenty of wait that's actually true moments. Agenda: Doors Open: 6:30 PM Lecture + Q&A: 6:45 PM - 8 PM Open-form networking: 8 PM & onwards Whether you're a parent, student, educator, or just someone fascinated by neuroscience, this is the perfect first night for PhDs & Pints. Smart people. Cold drinks. Big conversations.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Bets Over Baghdad
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7. Drinks included in ticket. Polymarket processed $3.6 billion on a single presidential race. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. They're the first honest reading of it we've ever had. One side says the market is the truth. The other says some truths shouldn't have a market. Lindsey Cormack, PhD, is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Stevens Institute of Technology & the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It). She runs DCinbox, which has archived every email Congress sends its constituents for over a decade, & contributes to the New York Times, Washington Post, Bloomberg, FiveThirtyEight, & Fox News. Kalshi just signed deals to pipe its odds into CNN & CNBC broadcasts. Bloomberg Terminal now carries prediction-market prices on the same screens as oil futures. The contracts run 24/7 the way commodities do: presidential races, congressional control, ceasefire dates, war casualty counts. A few clicks gets you long a candidate, short a hostage release, or a position on whether a sitting senator survives the year. Kalshi's CEO says the goal is to "financialize everything." He's most of the way there. So: are prediction markets the most honest reading of civic life we've ever built, or the corruption of every outcome they touch? For the prosecution, the answer is obvious. Some things shouldn't be priced. The moment you can profit from a war dragging on or an election going a particular way, you've created an incentive to make it so...and handed the deepest pockets in finance the keys to a democracy they were already overrepresented in. Markets that pay you for predicting an assassination attempt aren't predicting anything. They're paying people to think about it. A republic that lets citizens hedge against its own outcomes isn't a republic with better data. It's one that has quietly outsourced its civic life to traders. For the defense, that's squeamishness dressed as principle. These markets aggregate information better than polls, better than pundits, better than the press. They put skin in the game on claims that have lived consequence-free for decades. Banning them doesn't make wars or elections less consequential, it just hands price discovery to offshore platforms, foreign capital, & worse actors. Polymarket & Kalshi aren't corrupting civic life. events.name: AI & What Makes Us Human
events.description: Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI. We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly & effortlessly - the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, & the same songs, restaurants, & aesthetics rise to the top everywhere. What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict & automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human - our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives - turned into data, & data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, & it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us.  The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets & the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are. About Camille CarltonCamille is the Senior Director of Strategy & Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed & developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech & society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, & The New York Times, & her work has been published in Science & Tech Policy Press. About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, & ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, & career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline. Read our Responsible Tech Guide & numerous reports & guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings & livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, & attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here. About BrainStation BrainStation is the global leader in digital skills learning & workforce transformation. They empower businesses & professionals to succeed in the digital age by equipping them with the necessary skills to create value in fields such as AI, data, design, marketing & product. == PLEASE NOTE: We try to accept the right number of attendees to have a full event. Please arrive on time to ensure a seat, as the capacity is 100 people.

events.name: AI Comes To The Museum
events.description: Join Aboard for a conversation with Hlne Alonso of WonderWay, Spencer Kiser of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, & Danny Reynolds of the Museum of Modern Art as they discuss how museums & other cultural institutions are beginning to use artificial intelligence in both public-facing experiences & behind-the-scenes operations. From visitor engagement & collections to governance, infrastructure, & organizational change, they'll explore where AI is already proving useful, how organizations can design around its limitations, & what thoughtful adoption looks like in institutions built around knowledge, creativity, & public trust. Aboard president Paul Ford will moderate the discussion, followed by an audience Q&A. Afterward, stay for food, drinks, & conversation with the speakers & fellow attendees. About the speakers: Hlne Alonso is the founder of WonderWay, a conversational AI platform that transforms curated cultural knowledge into personalized conversations with visitors. WonderWay is currently being piloted at the MIT Museum as part of a research study with MIT Sloan. Hlne also teaches at NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program, where she explores AI, spatial experiences, & new forms of human-computer interaction. Her career has spanned both cultural institutions-including the American Museum of Natural History, the Wildlife Conservation Society, & Liberty Science Center-and the tech industry, where she served as Chief Design Officer at two Series B startups. Spencer Kiser is Senior Manager of Application Development at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, where he leads the team behind the Met's web platform & APIs, including the new semantic search experience. With over 20 years in cultural institutions, including MoMA & the American Museum of Natural History, his work has spanned in-gallery experiences, mobile development, API architecture, & the Met's Open Access initiative. His path winds through sound: field recording & sound design alongside a coding practice, shaped by NYU's Interactive Telecommunications Program & its culture of experimentation & collaboration. Outside work, he enjoys archiving physical media & hacking on hardware & local AI tooling. He lives in New York with his family. Danny Reynolds is an AI enablement leader at The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), where he helps deploy practical AI systems & enterprise technology that support one of the world's leading cultural institutions. Drawing on a background that spans a library & information science degree focusing on archives & records management to more than a decade at Apple, he focuses on the real-world challenges of AI adoption, governance, & organizational change.

Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQSome slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsReady to showcase your groundbreaking AI research, revolutionary AI use, or game-changing model? events.name: Newsweek AI Health Summit
events.description: Join us for the Newsweek AI Health Summit AI Health Summit: driving outcomes & reducing risk Artificial intelligence is starting to enable what American healthcare has long hoped to achieve: faster diagnoses, more personalized treatment & fewer operational & administrative hurdles. Yet despite its early impact, value remains uneven & difficult to scale. To bridge this gap, hospital leaders must move beyond isolated pilots toward system-wide AI deployment. This requires a fundamental shift in strategy: modernizing legacy infrastructure, establishing risk-based governance frameworks that empower clinicians rather than bypass them, & navigating a complex regulatory "patchwork"--250 state-level AI bills were introduced in 2025 alone, with 33 enacted across 21 states. How can health system leaders close the AI implementation gap while managing risk & earning clinical trust? What do landmark partnerships such as that between Nvidia & Eli Lilly's Co-Innovation lab mean for advancing drug discovery, & moving towards more effective & personalized treatments? Join Newsweek & Investment Reports for the AI Health Summit in New York City on September 23rd to learn how leading organizations are turning AI experimentation into impact.

events.name: The Great Founder River Float Of 2026
events.description: Join us on Saturday, August 22nd, 2026, for an unforgettable founder river float retreat on the Delaware River. events.name: Claude Code Workshop
events.description: Learn to orchestrate AI agents that write & ship code for you. Claude Code is already changing how the best engineering teams ship. This workshop, presented with Provectus, is a chance to build with it directly - not watch a demo, not sit through slides about it. You'll leave having shipped something real, with a working sense of how to bring this back to your own team. We'll spend a little time on context - how Claude Code fits into modern engineering workflows & where teams are seeing the biggest wins. Then the slides go away, & you're at a build station with Anthropic engineers & Provectus partners beside you, orchestrating agents that write & ship code while you direct the work.   Why attend Ship real output. Your agents write the code - you direct them. You'll leave with something you actually built, not a slide deck about what's possible. See best practices in action. Learn how Claude Code fits into enterprise workflows, from the people who deploy it at scale. Get direct support. Live help at every table from Anthropic engineers & Provectus partners - no one gets stuck on an error alone. Build your network. Spend the afternoon with technical leaders wrestling with the same questions you are.   Who should attend Engineering Leaders - EMs, VPs, CTOs, Platform Leads, Principal Engineers Business Leaders - CPOs, Digital Transformation, senior AI sponsors, PMs You don't need to be an engineer. If you're making decisions about AI investment or setting strategy, understanding what Claude Code actually does is the edge.   Agenda 1:00 PM - 2:30 PM: Registration & setup support 2:30 PM - 3:00 PM: Welcome, Claude Code overview, demo 3:00 PM - 5:00 PM: Build session: hands-on with Claude Code 4 PM - 5 PM: Networking Happy Hour   What to bring Your laptop - Basic comfort with a terminal or code editor is helpful but not required - you'll be directing AI agents & building alongside them, & our team supports you the whole way.   The fine print The event is free to attend if selected. Registration is required & subject to approval. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis - apply early. Want to bring a colleague? Have them apply separately - every seat needs its own approved registration.

events.name: Prediction Markets x Institutional Adoption
events.description: Join 51 Alpha in New York City for an evening exploring prediction markets as the new financial asset class & their growing role across finance, politics, & decision-making. The evening will bring together leaders with deep experience across prediction markets & institutional finance to discuss how the industry is evolving & what greater institutional participation could mean for the future of prediction markets. Following the panel & audience Q&A, join founders, traders, investors, policymakers, & industry leaders for a networking mixer. Schedule 4:00-4:30 PM - Networking4:30-4:35 PM - VERIFACT: Investor-backed startup out-of-stealth reveal4:35-5:05 PM - Prediction Markets Panel5:05-5:20 PM - Audience Q&A5:20-6:00 PM - Networking Mixer Presenting Sponsor: Verifact Markets - a platform where people can trade True or False on disputed facts. Think prediction markets, but instead of asking what will happen, we ask what has actually happened. Markets are resolved based on evidence, which anyone can review & contribute. Combining evidence analysis & market signals using a purpose-built AI system (patent-pending) to examine disputed claims at scale. Panelists John Aristotle Phillips - CEO of Aristotle & PredictIt. Phillips is one of the pioneers of modern prediction markets & founded PredictIt, one of the first widely used political prediction markets in the U.S. He has spent decades advancing forecasting markets as tools for better decision-making, public policy, & democratic transparency. A Princeton University graduate, he holds a B.S. in Aerospace Engineering. Dan M. Berkovitz - Vice Chairman for External & Regulatory Affairs at Millennium. Previously, Berkovitz served as General Counsel of the U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission, Commissioner of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, & General Counsel of the CFTC. While serving as CFTC General Counsel, he played a significant role in the formulation & implementation of the Dodd-Frank Act, including the development & implementation of the special rule governing event contracts. He is also a Lecturer in Law at Columbia Law School, where he teaches derivatives regulation. Moderator: Gina Antoniello - is Academic Director & Clinical Assistant Professor at the Tisch Institute for Global Sport at New York University-a leader working at the edge of sport, culture, & social impact. She brings over a decade inside professional sports, leading marketing-communications, social responsibility, & player development for globally recognized organizations including the Golden State Warriors & the Brooklyn Nets. Event Partners: Series Sponsors: Edge Markets & PredictItEcosystem Sponsor: Connamara Technologies Hosted by Aggie @BlondiePredicts Learn more about 51 Alpha & upcoming prediction markets events: fiftyonealpha.com Location & AttendanceThis is a curated event & attendance requires approval. The exact Midtown West location will be shared with approved guests only. Please register individually; no plus-ones unless separately approved. Photography & Video Notice Photography & videography will take place throughout the event. By attending, you acknowledge that you may appear in photographs or video recordings used by 51 Alpha for promotional, marketing, social media, editorial, & documentation purposes. If you prefer not to be photographed or recorded, please notify a member of the event team upon arrival.

events.name: Kubernetes Developers Meetup
events.description: Join the Elastic NYC User Group & Plural Kubernetes Developers on Tuesday, August 25th for an exciting meetup. We'll feature a presentation from Michael Guarino (Plural) & Eric Mustin (Elastic) followed by networking, refreshments, & pizza with the New York City tech community.  Date: Tuesday, August 25th from 6:00-8:00 PM Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup? Email us at [meetups@elastic.co](mailto:meetups@elastic.co)Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food6:00 pm: Talk # 1 - Details coming soon - Michael Guarino (Plural)7:00 pm: Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic - Eric Mustin (Elastic)7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up Talk Details:Telemetry's Long Way Home: A Kubernetes Odyssey with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic Eric Mustin (Elastic)Like Odysseus trying to find his way home, Kubernetes telemetry must navigate a difficult journey through dynamic workloads, short-lived infrastructure, overlapping tools, dropped signals, & unexpected operational monsters. This talk explores how Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, & Elastic can work together to give Kubernetes metrics, logs, & traces a reliable path home. We'll look at practical collection architectures, Prometheus-native metrics, OpenTelemetry processing & routing, & how Elastic can bring the resulting signals together. Along the way, we'll discuss resiliency, duplication, architectural tradeoffs, & how to avoid getting lost at sea in an increasingly complex observability ecosystem.

events.name: AI 2040 discussion: AI safety planning workshop
events.description:
We're still intending to run our forecasting event, but we're bumping it to later in September. In its place we've got something related, and also changed the date from August 19 to September 1.

The AI Futures Project (the team behind AI 2027) has published its most ambitious work yet: AI 2040: Plan A, a scenario in which the US and China strike a deal in 2029 to avoid a reckless race to superintelligence. The world pauses AI capabilities at top-human-expert level in 2035, and scales to superintelligence only in 2040, under total research transparency and a regime the authors call Mutually Assured Compute Destruction. The authors are explicit that this is a recommendation rather than a prediction, and that they wrote it as an exercise in "scenario scrutiny": most AI policy proposals fall apart when you try to write down a detailed world in which they succeed. Our job for the evening is to apply that same scrutiny to Plan A itself.

We'll spend most of the evening in small-group discussion, working through the scenario's timelines, the deal mechanics, the rival plans (B, C, D, and S), and where Plan A is most likely to break. We'll finish with a forecast round in which each group registers probabilities on a handful of concrete questions about how the next few years actually unfold, and we compare the spread across the room.

Please read the whole scenario at ai-2040.com over the weekend before the event if you can; it's long but reads quickly, and the later chapters reward the effort. If you're pushed for time, about 30 minutes covers the essentials: the introductory front matter, the 2029 "Choose a Path" chapter, and a skim of 2027 and 2028. Here is a handout with the schedule and discussion questions in advance, and we'll have spare copies (and a cheat sheet for anyone who couldn't do the reading) on the night. Newcomers are very welcome.

Getting here: We're on the 3rd floor of 26 Broadway, in the Primary coworking space (map). Enter the building, go down the stairs, turn right to the elevators, and take the set of elevators on your right. Someone will be at the door to meet you.

Schedule: Doors at 6:30pm, discussion 7:00 to 8:40, then networking and socializing.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Turning Towards Our Invisible Selves
events.description:
“The truth is we are One. The reality is we are not.”
- Leticia Nieto, Understanding Oppression
Turning toward what is difficult and challenging in our relationships is a powerful way to meet the seemingly unaddressable challenges of our society. As we turn toward the places of fear and discomfort in ourselves and in our relationships, we build the capacity to turn toward the mirrors of those same issues in our culture and our world. This can include the ways we relate to our own identities like age, race, culture, education, economic status, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, and more.
We don't have to come from defeat, anger, misunderstanding, or powerlessness in order to do the social activism of acknowledging and loving these pieces of ourselves. In the midst of doing the real work of paying attention to the things we usually ignore, we can be supported by delight, laughter, joy, and lightheartedness. We'll weave together reverence for these “invisible selves” and the delightful play that comes from not taking ourselves too seriously. We don't know exactly what will come up between us in this workshop — but we know we're up for the adventure of finding out.
“We don’t have to know the answers. We just have to choose to live into the truth”
- Reverend Angel Kyodo Williams

Agenda
9:30am - doors open, arrival
10am - doors close
Morning - a guided interactive small-group activity to bring awareness to the implicit dynamics between us and the ways that we often feel misunderstood or unseen
12-1 - catered lunch
Afternoon - a facilitated group process to clear some of the content that is ready to be cleared (up to you how deep you want to go). We’ll then move into guided activities around creativity and play, and a guided meditation to help integrate the process we just moved through
Event details
Everything will be taught from the basics – all you need is to be curious
Everything is opt-in and your “no” will always be honored
You can come alone or with a friend
All you’ll need is a journal, a pen, and a water bottle. Lunch is included, accommodating for dietary restrictions.
Spots at this workshop are limited to maintain the size necessary for small group work, so we’d recommend getting your ticket as soon as you know you’d like to come
If you need a need-based scholarship to be able to attend, please reach out to info@sleepawake.camp.
Facilitator: Sarah Cruse

Sarah has been with Sleepawake since 2023, leading both our emotional and relational curriculum and our creative expression curriculum at almost every retreat we’ve ever run. As a young repressed and depressed adult, trying to find her way out of patterns of personal and familial trauma, she found poetry and discovered the healing power of embodied truth, authentic voice and creative expression. Through spoken word, theater, singing, and sound exploration, she discovered an internal river of emergence. It is a deep listening, a profound wellspring of self-expression, a pathway towards healing that changed her life forever. Sarah now supports people and communities in activating their own inner creative pathways. Outside of Sleepawake, she is currently a practitioner of energetic medicine, sound healing and trauma clearing, and the lead singer of her band Yaya's Kitchen. Sarah is up for the adventure of whatever this day together brings and delighted to be part of it with you.
About SleepaWeek
Sleepawake is coming to NYC for a week! Check out our events calendar to see everything happening this week. If the ticket price is a blocker to your attendance, please reach out to info@sleepawake.camp for details on need-based scholarship discounts.

events.description:
Every single person has had some sad and kinda awful stuff happen to them. Also some funny stuff. Also some stuff they don't know how to feel about. Let's share in the totality of how varied and strange it is to be a human!

After meeting one another and settling in, we’ll spend most of our time on an activity where you get to see others and be seen one layer (or more?) deeper than you might normally. This one's sweet, and tender, and funny, and...I think it's easier for me to like you now.
Doors open at 7 and close at 7:15 sharp; please be there before 7:15 to participate in this one.

About your facilitator

Raven is a facilitator and curriculum builder at Sleepawake. She brings almost a decade of somatic, relational, and emotional work to the room. Previously a medic, filmmaker, tech worker, and hardcore meditator (accumulating four months in silent meditation including a stint in a monastery in Myanmar), her work now draws from various meditation traditions: Vipassana (Goenka, Gaya House traditions) and Mahamudra (Rigdzin with Dustin DiPerna). It also incorporates teachings from Realization Process (where she's a certified teacher, trained with Judith Blackstone and Roma Hammel), the Conscious Leadership Group (she's a certified 15 Commitments Coach, trained with Jim Dethmer and Diana Chapman), and a body of work that treats emotions as energy to be welcomed rather than managed, with enjoyment as the accelerator of change. Having worked with hundreds of people, Raven knows the stuff we most want to skip is usually the stuff worth staying with, and she makes this difficult task feel like a bold and wild ride.
For anyone who wants to access more personal freedom, to be honest about what they want, and to turn the most "bad" and difficult aspects of themselves into allies and heroes - Raven's got you.
At home in Berkeley, you might find her hanging out with her beautiful besties, playing narrative-driven video games and getting absolutely shredded at the gym.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Conflict as a Compass
events.description:
The strongest relationships aren't conflict avoidant; they're skilled and practiced at repair.
Ever find yourself flailing when a relationship is in conflict — robotically reciting Nonviolent Communication scripts, giving in and abandoning yourself, or walking away?
Conflict, when held a certain way, can be a clear signal of what we want for ourselves and the people we love. Its pain can be a motivating and energizing force, pointing us towards deeper, more honest relationships with ourselves and others. It's simple, but not always easy.

"Sleepawake challenged me to be more real than I ever have been, and guided me towards acting radically in alignment with my truth. It's not at all easy, but the more I do this, the more I feel like my life is ripe with possibility."
You'll leave this workshop with:
A new framework for understanding what conflict is, why it comes up, and how it can improve (rather than destroy) relationships
Real practice diving into building understanding and repair, in a real conflict that's present in your life (up to you how spicy you want to go)
A set of tools you can bring to future difficult conversations without sounding like a robot trying to say the right thing to make the conflict go away
Whether you're a Sleepawake alum or never attended one of our events, this workshop is for you if you're wanting to expand your relational toolbox to include real, authentic, vulnerable, unscripted conflict repair.
This workshop will be adapted directly from our Conflict module at Sleepawake Immersive, our weeklong intensive program. We'll spend just enough time on theory to understand the territory we're entering, and then we'll spend the majority of the time on interactive exercises including journaling, small group work, and full-group discussion.


If you'd like to do this workshop in person with friends, you'll have the option to do the small group work portion together. You're just as welcome to come on your own; this workshop is designed for you to build skills that will support all your relationships beyond this evening.
In order to maintain an intimate group for this event with enough space for facilitated group discussion, we will be capping admission.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] Freezestylin'
events.description:
Creativity isn’t limited to our abilities to paint a nice picture or dance in the coolest way — it’s the skill underlying innovation. Fundamentally, it is the ability to build something out of nothing, whether that thing is a product or a business or a song you sing in the shower.
You’ll leave this event with quicker and easier access to your creative prowess — which you can channel directly into any part of your life in need of creative problem solving.
This night is designed for laughter and curiosity, not performing or being "good" at art.
“Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up.” - Picasso
As children, all of us knew how to sing and dance and draw without worrying about whether it was good enough. As we grow up, most of us learn to censor our own creative impulses, only building when we are confident we can create something good. In doing so, we block ourselves off from our own creative abilities, and lose out on our grandest ideas and innovations.
Tonight, we’ll use the voice as our medium to train our long-unused creative muscles. We’ll start gently. Although all of us knew as children how to sing and dance like no one’s watching, most of us have now learned that we have to be good at creativity in order to be comfortable accessing it. Through wordplay, rhythm, and singing games, we’ll slowly open to the possibility that we can create badly (and to the fun that ensues) — which, counterintuitively, unblocks more access to our creativity and our ability to create well.
This is not built for professional artists — this event is for people who are excited about the idea of having more access to creative thinking in their day-to-day lives, and who are open to (and probably also intimidated by) the idea of rapping or singing as part of structured games in a group of amateurs.
“Remember, before you can be great, you’ve got to be good. Before you can be good, you’ve got to be bad. But before you can even be bad, you’ve got to try.” - Art Williams
Everything we offer at this event will be opt-in. We will never make you get up on stage in front of everyone — we’ll never push you to doing any part of this that you don’t want to do. This night is for you, and we are in full support of your choices about how you’d like to participate.
Our facilitation team has been running this event for over four years, and they are familiar with both the joy and the fear that people often feel around creative expression.
Agenda
Settling in & short introduction to creative access as a trainable skill
Individual freestyle word-play games — no one will be listening to you
Group-based low-stakes voice and rhythm games — focused on the joy of what’s created, whether good or terrible
Group-based singing games — sweet, gentle, and facilitated by our team to support you in participating to exactly whatever extent you’d like to
Open-ended time to hang out and join or listen to a jam session
Logistics
There are limited spots at this event, and we will not take walk-ins if it sells out — we have a specific cap on attendance so that we can accommodate breakout groups with our facilitation team
You may want a water bottle; no need to bring anything else
Please arrive on time and plan to stay for the duration of the event; the evening is a full arc where each activity builds on the previous one
Come solo or with friends

events.name: SideQuest IRL #52
events.description:
Join us for an afternoon of pursuing your personal side quest! Whether you’re writing, coding, or doing those taxes you’ve been putting off, this is your space. It’s intentional time for you to focus on what feels meaningful to you—and meet people doing the same thing. We’ll split our time between focused work sessions and breaks to reset and mingle with other creators.
Rough Agenda*
2:30-3:00pm: Introductions and Intention Sharing
3:00-4:30pm: Deep focus session 1
4:30-4:50pm: Optional break
4:50-5:30pm: Deep focus session 2
5:30-6:00pm: SideQuest Shares
*Popular opinion is that SideQuest is best when you’re all in, showing up for the duration instead of splitting sessions. Try it—we think you’ll agree.
___________________

About SideQuest:
We host coworking sessions every other Sunday. Subscribe to our events calendar if you can’t make this one :)
If you've got ideas for how to help build the community, or you'd like to host a future SideQuest (it's easier than you might think!), we'd love to hear from you.
Thank you to Fractal Campus for hosting us, our friends at PurdueHackers, CozySundays and Socratica for seeding the idea, and Chandiran for building the SideQuest community.

events.name: Synthesizer Night @ NYC Resistor
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/synthesizer-night-nyc-resistor-tickets-1997646041084

Gathering musicians, enthusiasts, and curious minds to connect, collaborate, and share their passion for synthesis. BYO synth encouraged!Join us at NYC Resistor, a makerspace in Brooklyn for an electrifying Synthesizer Night! Get ready to unleash your creativity, explore sonic landscapes, and connect with fellow synth enthusiasts in an evening dedicated to the mesmerizing world of synthesizers. This is a pay-what-you-wish event (recommended donation $8).
Synthesizer Night at NYC Resistor is a celebration of all things synthesizer. Whether you're a seasoned musician, an avid collector, or simply fascinated by the possibilities of electronic sound, this event offers a unique opportunity to gather with like-minded individuals and revel in the captivating soundscape of synthesizers.
At Synthesizer Night, participants are encouraged to bring their own synthesizers, from vintage analog gems to cutting-edge modular wonders. It's a chance to showcase your personal setup, experiment with new equipment, and dive into the rich sonic tapestry that synthesizers offer.
For those looking to enhance the collaborative experience, consider arriving early to connect your synthesizer to a MIDI/CV clock. This allows for synchronized timing among all instruments, creating a seamless musical fusion during impromptu jam sessions.
In addition to the collaborative jam sessions, the event provides a unique opportunity for a show and tell/play with anything that attendees bring. Share your favorite gear, experiment with different setups, and engage in hands-on exploration of various synthesizers and electronic music equipment.
The event unfolds in a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere, providing a platform for musicians, enthusiasts, and curious minds to connect, collaborate, and share their passion for synthesis. Whether you're a beginner seeking guidance or an expert eager to inspire others, Synthesizer Night is the perfect setting to engage in conversations, exchange knowledge, and foster a vibrant community. 
Throughout the evening, you'll have the opportunity to engage in impromptu jam sessions, where the collective energy of multiple synthesizers intertwines to create awe-inspiring sounds. Experience the joy of collaborating with fellow musicians, experiment with different genres and styles, and let the unique characteristics of each instrument shape your sonic explorations.
Additionally, for those who wish to showcase their skills and perform, there will be dedicated performance slots. Take center stage, captivate the audience, and let your creativity soar as you demonstrate the full potential of your synthesizer setup. To sign up for a performance slot, email classes@nycresistor.com or join our Discord and post to #synth.
Whether you're an ardent synth enthusiast, an aspiring musician, or simply curious about the captivating world of synthesizers, Synthesizer Night at NYC Resistor is an event that will inspire, educate, and leave you in awe of the boundless possibilities that electronic sound offers. Don't miss this opportunity to immerse yourself in an evening of music, collaboration, and innovation. Mark your calendars, pack up your favorite synths, and join us at NYC Resistor for a night you won't soon forget. We can't wait to see you there!
This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.

events.name: Learn to Use a Fiber Laser Cutter to Etch Your Own Designs in Metal
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/learn-to-use-a-fiber-laser-cutter-to-etch-your-own-designs-in-metal-tickets-1994965147459

Harness the power of an Xtool Fiber Laser! In this class you'll learn everything you need.Learn to Use a Fiber Laser Cutter to Etch Your Own Designs in MetalIn this class you'll learn everything you need to know to make the ideas in your head become a reality with a fiber laser.In this three hour class, you will learn:- How to set up a file for fiber laser etching in Inkscape or Adobe Illustrator.- Fiber laser safety including materials testing.- Fiber laser operation including configuration, focus, and etching on common metals like stainless steel, aluminum, brass, and others.At the end of class, you will go home with:- One etched metal project, either the class default or a simple one of your own design (see below for details)- Resistor Laser Certification, enabling you to use our fiber laser on Craft Nights.Please bring the following to class:- A laptop with either Inkscape (free: download here: https://inkscape.org/release/inkscape-1.2.1/) or Adobe Illustrator installed.- A USB jump drivePrerequisite: You must have completed our CO2 Laser Safety class before taking this course. If you haven't taken it yet, you will be asked to do so before attending. Sign up early to secure your spot in both.The following items are optional if you'd like to try a custom design. If your file ends up being too complicated, we may have you do the class default project first, just to learn the laser in the time allotted — but we'll definitely help you with your more complex etch at a free Craft Night in future!
- An SVG vector file of a simple design you'd like to etch.- A metal item you'd like to etch (tumbler, keychain, tag, etc.). If you can't bring your own material, small pieces will be made available, or larger pieces for purchase on site.

events.name: NYCResistor Ham Radio Club
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/nycresistor-ham-radio-club-tickets-1633091413379

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.
Come make some noise in the weird and wonderful medium of radio!This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.
Please note that refunds must be requested 24 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

events.name: SideQuest IRL #44
events.description:
Join us for an afternoon of pursuing your personal side quest! Whether you’re writing, coding, or doing those taxes you’ve been putting off, this is your space. It’s intentional time for you to focus on what feels meaningful to you—and meet people doing the same thing. We’ll split our time between focused work sessions and breaks to reset and mingle with other creators.
Rough Agenda*
2:30-3:00pm: Introductions and Intention Sharing
3:00-4:30pm: Deep focus session 1
4:30-4:50pm: Optional break
4:50-5:30pm: Deep focus session 2
5:30-6:00pm: SideQuest Shares
*Popular opinion is that SideQuest is best when you’re all in, showing up for the duration instead of splitting sessions. Try it—we think you’ll agree.
___________________

About SideQuest:
We host coworking sessions every other Sunday. Subscribe to our events calendar if you can’t make this one :)
If you've got ideas for how to help build the community, or you'd like to host a future SideQuest (it's easier than you might think!), we'd love to hear from you.
Thank you to Fractal Campus for hosting us, our friends at PurdueHackers, CozySundays and Socratica for seeding the idea, and Chandiran for building the SideQuest community.
