events.name: Cozy Sundays — Summer '26 Session VII
events.description:
Summer is here, and every fortnight we gather again for Cozy Sundays. You know the drill.
house rules
To enter the space, buzz Ambrook and take the stairs. If you have accessibility needs, message a host for elevator access (key fob required)
The buzzer will be muted after 2:30, as it is quite loud. Please come on time to avoid disrupting the quiet work periods, and to ensure you can get in.
Bring snacks or tea to share, or a suggested donation to the snack fund to continue to support cozy sundays <3
The office has rooms, but they are not soundproof. So please refrain from taking calls during this session as there is limited phone booth availability.
Ambrook is a shoes-off office! Wear your best socks :)
Please only RSVP if you can make it and stay the whole time.
schedule
2-2:30p: arrive, quick primer on the session, intros circle
2:30-3:30p: deep work session #1
3:30-3:45: break
3:45-4:45p: deep work session #2
4:45-5:30: demos - sharing ideas, works in progress, and celebrating wins
5:30-6:00: mingle & wrap up
~ optional ~ some of us grab dinner after!
About Cozy Sundays
We exist to support people as they work on the things that they love but struggle to make time for — this place is not for job hunting, catching up on work, sending emails, making sales pitches or networking.
We fiercely protect what makes each session special because the magic only exists when we all buy in together.
Thank you Ambrook for lending us their space. Ambrook is building the financial layer powering American industry. They are hiring across roles in engineering, growth and sales.
If you can't make it this time but are interested in attending a future session 👉 subscribe to the events calendar lu.ma/cozy-sundays

events.name: Satori Book Club Vol. 2: Choose Your Adventure
events.description:
A chill book club for ambitious people who want to read interesting books, have better conversations, and make life a little more interesting.
Welcome to Satori Book Club: Vol. 2.
We’ll spend the afternoon hanging out in the park, geeking out on interesting ideas, sharing spicy takes, debating the things we disagree on, and inevitably going down a few completely unnecessary rabbit holes along the way.
📚 What we're reading
Main Book
The Alchemist — Paulo Coelho
A short philosophical story about following your dreams, trusting your gut, and figuring out what you actually want out of life. Plenty to debate around destiny, purpose, risk, and whether the universe is actually trying to tell you something.
⚔️ Fiction Side Quest
Dungeon Crawler Carl — Matt Dinniman
Earth gets turned into a giant intergalactic dungeon game show, and a dude named Carl has to survive it with his ex-girlfriend’s cat. It’s absurd, hilarious, surprisingly deep, and apparently extremely hard to put down once you start.
🤝 Business / Self-Improvement Side Quest
Never Split the Difference — Chris Voss
Written by a former FBI hostage negotiator, this one is all about communicating and negotiating when the stakes are high. Lots of practical ideas for business, relationships, and everyday life.
Quick reminder: You really don’t have to read the books — read one, read them all, read half, or come in completely blind. The books are really just fuel for interesting ideas, deep conversations, spicy takes, and random rabbit holes. No pressure, no homework vibes.
We started this thing so we could geek out on deep ideas, philosophy, and life’s big questions together instead of having all those conversations in our own heads. 🧠
We’ll be meeting at Sheep Meadow in Central Park. Bring something comfortable to sit on, a snack if you'd like, and come ready to hang.
A rough idea of the afternoon:
👋 Hang out and catch up
📚 Break into groups around the different books and discussion prompts
🌶️ Share insights, hot takes, disagreements, and whatever rabbit holes we find ourselves in
🗳️ Nominate + vote on what we read next
🌳 Stick around afterward to hang, read, or enjoy the park
Every ~6 weeks we’ll pick some new books, get together to talk about them, and sprinkle in casual reading hangs and other shenanigans in between.
If you like interesting people, interesting ideas, and conversations that go a little deeper than “so, what do you do?” — come hang. 📚🤙

events.name: AI and What Makes Us Human, a Fireside Chat with Camille Carlton + Responsible Tech Mixer
events.description:
Join All Tech Is Human's founder, David Ryan Polgar, for a fireside chat with Center for Humane Technology's Camille Carlton about what it means to be human in the age of AI.
We're told AI will give us everything we want, instantly and effortlessly — the perfect playlist, the ideal trip, the answer to any question.But a decade of algorithmic recommendation systems already showed us what happens when a handful of platforms decide what culture we see: our tastes narrow, our choices converge, and the same songs, restaurants, and aesthetics rise to the top everywhere.

What's less visible is why. To build a system that can predict and automate what we want, AI companies need something from us first: the intangible, hard-to-quantify parts of being human — our words, our habits, our relationships, our inner lives — turned into data, and data into product. This is the monetization of the human experience, and it's the engine behind the frictionless world being sold to us. 

The more of ourselves we hand over, the more "effortless" the system gets and the less room is left for the friction that actually makes us who we are.

About Camille Carlton
Camille is the Senior Director of Strategy and Impact at Center for Humane Technology, where she shapes organizational strategy to ensure technology is designed and developed in the public interest. Recognized as one of Business Insider's AI 100 in 2023, Camille works at the cutting edge of the biggest debates in tech and society. Camille has been featured in Bloomberg, NBC News, and The New York Times, and her work has been published in Science and Tech Policy Press.
About All Tech Is Human
All Tech Is Human is a non-profit organization that provides a sandbox for solution-building and socialization to influence key levers of change. We take a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackle thorny tech & society issues, shape the Responsible Tech movement, and ensure that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. Our activities span three key areas: multistakeholder community-building, educational resources, and career-related activities to help diversify the pipeline.
Read our Responsible Tech Guide and numerous reports and guides, join our Slack community of 15k members across 115 countries, attend our in-person gatherings and livestreams, participate in our working groups, utilize our Responsible Tech Job Board, take our new Responsible AI courses, and attend our Responsible Tech Summit (in-person & virtual) on October 29. See all of our projects here.

At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, and emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, and design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust?
The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a highly curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align and shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, and philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. events.name: In Common(s): A screening of the documentary “L’Asilo, Creating Space for Care” with 8-Ball Community
events.description:
L’Asilo, Creating Space for Care is a documentary focused on the commons space the Ex Asilo Filangeri, located in the heart of Napoli, which will be used as a basis for comparison with the volunteer-run artist collective 8-Ball, located in New York.
Conversation with Silvia Lucia Cohn and Lele Saveri to follow.
8-Ball Community is proud to partner with Index to screen the film L’Asilo: Creating Space for Care, a documentary that tells the story of the commons space L’Asilo, based in Naples. Focusing on a time of change in their history, this documentary examines the structure, pitfalls ,and progress this artists' collective has gone through.
There are parallels evident between L’Asilo and 8-Ball Community, and we want this screening to begin a dialogue about what it means to be a part of these kinds of spaces.
Stick around after the film for a conversation between Silvia Lucia Cohn, an inhabitant of L’Asilo featured in the film, and Lele Saveri, founder of 8-Ball Community.
Program
Doors at 7:00pm, screening at 7:30pm (50 minute runtime) with conversation to follow.
Facilitators

Silvia Lucia Cohn is a designer who works on eco-social projects and is specialized in designing and facilitating participatory processes. She also has experience in education and activism that overlap with her work as well as personal time.
Silvia has been an inhabitant/activist of L’Asilo since 2022. She is from New York but of Neapolitan origin, specifically from Procida and Ischia.


Lele Saveri is an Italian-born photographer and community organizer based in New York City.
Saveri’s work has been exhibited in various institutions, including MoMA (New York), FOAM (Amsterdam), MARCO (Rome), the Brooklyn Museum, among others.
In 2012, Saveri co-founded 8-Ball Community, an art collective and non-hierarchical organization that supports independent art and self-publishing in New York City and beyond.


Nicolas Umpierrez is an artist from Queens, New York City who focuses on work with the still and moving image. With a practice that varies from analogue photography to digital filmmaking, he is fascinated by the recorded image.
Since 2022 he’s been involved with 8-Ball Community, particularly with 8-Ball Television programming original content for the 8-Ball TV website and putting together community screenings.


8-Ball Community began as a series of parties in the Grand Billiards pool hall in Williamsburg, Brooklyn circa 2012. What first started out as a series of parties for their friends to come together, play music, exchange work (usually zines) and ideas grew into an organic network of artists and activists who would organize events around shared goals and ambitions. 8-Ball Community continues to expand today.

events.name: A Poem Is a Drawing, A Photo of a Friend: A Poetry Workshop
events.description:
Explore poetry as a medium of multitudes: Something of excess, something deeply personal, something widely shared.
Poetry is a free-use of language, a use of words outside of communicative utility: A poem uses language superfluously, gratuitously, sharply, round-about-ly. Too often we base our experience of writing in the concrete. Beauty is a thing of excess, of chance, and we’d do good to explore poetry as such.
Exploring the absurdity of language and experience through writing prompts, students will weave through solo and group exercises, leaving with seedlings of works to be sprouted. We will end the session with a communal tea time with light refreshments.
This workshop is built on play as praxis, open to all levels.
Program
Part 1: Lubrication Students will free-journal for five minutes.
Part 2: Know Thy Neighbor Writing poetry itself is an individual journey, but the familiarity with the world and people around us bring ease to putting sentiments on the page. A friendly environment is conducive to creativity!
Part 3: Free Association Students will begin with independent writing exercises that evolve to a group Exquisite Corpse exercise.
Part 4: Making a Poem Employing the whisper of ideas from the exercises, students will begin constructing a poem.
Part 6: Communion / Open Studio Students will have the opportunity to share what they have written. We will conclude with some communal time with light refreshments, having a chance to continue working in the space independently.
Resources
Acid Horizon Podcast, From Blake to Bataille: Romantisicm, Communism, and the Commons with Joseph Albernaz
Byung Chul-Han, Saving Beauty
Excerpt from D.W. Winnicott’s Home is Where We Start From, Living Creatively
Anna Crooks, Two Hole Poems
Facilitator

Ayaka Takao (she/they) is a New York based teaching artist and facilitator, born in Japan and raised in Honolulu, HI. With a primary interest in humanity, harmony, and love, Takao works across a diversity of mediums, employing of ceramics, painting, written word, and the World Wide Web.

events.name: [SleepaWeek NYC] What Fills My Cup?
events.description:
Our ability to meet life's challenges is capped by our emotional capacity. It's much easier to handle an upset roommate or a friend cancelling on us when we're feeling well-rested and grounded than when we're already overwhelmed. By deepening our ability to ground and resource ourselves, we can expand our emotional capacity — and with it, meet more of life's challenges.
Join us for a sweet, gentle evening of building emotional capacity through guided activities. What fills my cup? What drains me? How can I find rhythms of resource in my relationships?
You'll leave with tools for resourcing yourself emotionally in the context of relationships — and maybe feeling like you just got a long professional massage, or lunch with an old friend.


Agenda
Short introduction
A simple yet powerful tool for peer support when you're feeling overwhelmed
An activity on learning about your own desires, beliefs, and needs in relationships
A guided meditation on resourcing and grounding
Event details
Please bring a yoga mat or anything else that will help you feel comfy and cozy for the lying down portion.
You are welcome to come alone or with friends.
Everything we offer at this workshop will be an opt-in invitation, and your no will always be honored.
About Your Facilitator: Sarah Cruse

Sarah has been with Sleepawake since 2023, leading both our emotional and relational curriculum and our creative expression curriculum at almost every retreat we’ve ever run. As a young repressed and depressed adult, trying to find her way out of patterns of personal and familial trauma, she found poetry and discovered the healing power of embodied truth, authentic voice and creative expression. Sarah now supports people and communities in activating their own inner creative pathways. Outside of Sleepawake, she is currently a practitioner of energetic medicine, sound healing and trauma clearing, and the lead singer of her band Yaya's Kitchen. Sarah is up for the adventure of whatever this evening together brings and delighted to be part of it with you.

events.name: Shape/Shift: The Artist's Way, In Practice + 1:1 Coaching
events.description:
A 12-week method to manifest your creative dreams, break through blocks, build empowering habits and put your work out there through The Artist's Way, Jungian philosophy, personalized coaching, and a supportive community of fellow artists.
Welcome! By landing on this page, you've received a digital invitation from the universe to take your creativity to a new, more abundant level. This will be our fourth cohort at Index, and over the last three, we've manifested some very cool and very real things. We're talking new careers, early retirements, confidence through the roof, limitless self-love, homes abroad, deep relationships, getting rich off our art, and a beautiful community that continues to uplift and inspire each other to shine as our true creative selves in our everyday lives.
The Artist's Way is a book designed to unlock your creative potential through tried-and-true exercises and a bit of manifestation magic. But Shape/Shift is much more than a book club. We're a collective, and your membership is valid indefinitely.
To be clear, you do not need to be an artist to participate. Creativity is a birthright. You choose how you express yourself, and if you don't know what ignites your spark, this course will help you figure that out, too.
During the course, we meet once a week to work through The Artist's Way. We'll discover more about ourselves and who we want to be, while also developing our community and fostering new creative relationships. Some weeks, we'll have guest speakers for extra inspiration, and other weeks, we'll dive into special activities like meditative birdwatching or zine-making. To practice your practice, each member of the cohort will have an opportunity to host a workshop of their own, and the course culminates in a group art show party for you to display your work and invite your loved ones to celebrate you. We check in daily and use our vibrant digital community (a WhatsApp Group) to hold each other accountable and create space for what comes up through the course and beyond. Additionally, you'll meet with Ella for 1:1 creative coaching sessions to help you conjure, set, and achieve your creative goals.
The goal is for you to go beyond your aspirations and have the audacity to overcome perfectionism and put your work out there in the world. Ella’s role is to support you in that, practically and spiritually.
You can join us IRL at Index in NYC, or dial in via Zoom. We've found a method that seamlessly integrates our digital and in-person cohorts. And if you're usually with us IRL but traveling that week, you can join digitally and stay accountable to your practice.
What you get:
13 class gatherings to connect, share + bloom with the cohort
1:1 creative coaching session and development of a 3-month project plan for you to execute on to bring your ideas to life
4 Q&As with alumni who've manifested creative abundance
Extracurricular activities such as birdwatching, cyanotyping, vision boarding, drinks & dinners
Lifetime access to the digital community + free meetups
Option to host your own workshop or skill presentation with production support from Ella
Option to participate in a group gallery show/party
Additional coaching, production support, and materials may have separate costs.
Beyond the course, our cohorts stay intact. We meet for dinner parties worldwide, collaborate on projects, and use the digital community to chat it up, share success, and ask for support. The magic is limitless.

Index Access
To deepen the sense of community within this cohort, Index is offering free coworking at Index Greenpoint to all registered students on days when class is held. We'll reach out the week before class starts to get you set up.

Scholarship & Teacher's Assistant
Index scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, and those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.
Additionally, we provide one scholarship for a teacher's assistant who is able to attend class in person each week and assist with AV and class logistics. You can apply for the TA position by emailing ciao@loverllc.com.

Syllabus
September 16 – Week 1 – Developing a Sense of Safety
Establish a safe and nurturing environment for creative exploration.
Introduce the course and its objectives.
Discuss key concepts from "The Artist's Way."
Journaling: Reflect on personal creative fears and aspirations.
September 23 – Week 2 – Developing a Sense of Identity
Define and embrace your unique artistic identity.
Discuss the importance of self-identity in the creative process.
Explore relevant essays from "The Artist's Way."
Journaling: Explore personal boundaries, needs, and desires.
September 30 – Week 3 – Developing a Sense of Power
Alumni Q&A #1
Embrace your creative power and break free from limiting beliefs.
Examine bursts of energy and emotional peaks in creative expression.
Study the concept of open mindfulness and its application in art.
October 7 – Week 4 – Developing a Sense of Integrity
Cultivate self-awareness and integrate newfound insights.
Discuss the concept of integrity in creative work.
Reflect on essays about self-definition.
Journaling: Document personal introspections and revelations.
October 14 – Week 5 – Developing the Sense of Possibility
Extracurricular: Vision boarding
Break free from self-imposed limitations and explore creative potential.
Analyze personal payoffs and limitations in creativity.
Discuss chapters about expanding possibilities.
Journaling: Identify areas where you've limited your creative potential.
October 21 – Week 6 – Developing a Sense of Abundance
Alumni Q&A #2
Shift perspectives on creative abundance and address money-related blocks.
Explore the relationship between creativity and financial abundance.
Reflect on creative blocks related to money.
Reflect on personal attitudes toward money and luxury.
October 24 –  Extracurricular – Birdwatching walk
October 28 – Week 7 – Developing a Sense of Connection
Deepen creative receptivity and engage with personal dreams.
Discuss the importance of receptivity and connection in creativity.
Discuss essays about connecting with creative interests.
Journaling: Document your genuine creative interests and dreams.
November 4 – Week 8 – Developing a Sense of Strength
Overcome time-related obstacles and empower your creative journey.
Explore time-related challenges and creative blocks.
Reflect on sections addressing time management.
Identify practical changes to make more time for creativity.
November 7 - Extracurricular - Cyanotyping
November 11 – Week 9 – Developing a Sense of Compassion
Alumni Q&A #3
Heal emotional wounds and cultivate self-compassion in the creative process.
Discuss internal blocks to creativity and emotional difficulties.
Explore healing and compassion.
Journaling: Address past failures and embrace self-compassion.
November 18 – Week 10 – Developing a Sense of Self-Protection
Identify and overcome toxic patterns that hinder creativity.
Explore common obstacles and toxic patterns in creative work.
Discuss strategies for protecting your creative process.
Reflect on personal toxic patterns and ways to break free.
No class November 25 — Wednesday before Thanksgiving
November 25 – Extracurricular – Gratitude dinner party for those in town
December 2 – Week 11 – Developing a Sense of Autonomy
Nurture your artistic self and develop behaviors that enhance creativity.
Discuss the importance of self-nurturing and autonomy in creativity.
Reflect on nurturing the artist within.
Journaling: Document behaviors that strengthen your creative journey.
December 9 – Week 12 – Developing a Sense of Faith
Alumni Q&A #4
Cultivate trust in the creative process and overcome last-minute doubts.
Explore the relationship between creativity and trust.
Set creative aims to bring with you into the new chapter of your creative process!
December 16 – Closing Session – Metamorphosis
Cohort-led workshop series begins (running through late December/early January)
Celebrate the transformation of the cohort and close out the book together.
January 16, 2027 (TBC) – Shape/Shift Gallery Show
Public showcase of cohort work, open to loved ones

Learning Outcomes
Overcome perfectionism
Build confidence and audacity
Identify goals
Practice your work
Share your work

Resources
The Artist's Way by Julia Cameron

Instructor Bio

Ella Fitch is a creative spiritualist and award-winning producer living between Brooklyn, NY and Venice, Italy. She is the founder of Lover LLC, where she hosts creative retreats, produces community events, leads courses on taking artistic leaps and works with individuals and businesses as a creative coach.
She’s produced documentaries, commercials, political campaigns, music festivals, experiential events, websites, apps, a few hundred meals at the soup kitchen, many dinner parties and probably a thousand poems.  All this has made her an expert in identifying a creative vision and developing the path to its success. She can talk endlessly about the connection between quantum physics and spirituality, your dog, Carl Jung, the taste of wild figs, how Venice looks under a full moon, and the democratization of art.
You can grab copy of her recent book of poems at Index, view a list of awards she’s received on her website, and book a free consultation for creative coaching with her.

More than 2 weeks before the program begins → 50% refund
Fewer than 2 weeks before the program begins → No refund
Thanks for understanding and for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase.

events.name: Intro to Soldering Workshop: Make an LED Tile
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/intro-to-soldering-workshop-make-an-led-tile-tickets-1998510904915

Soldering is one of the most important skills you'll need for working with electronics. Come join us for an introductory through-hole solderSoldering is one of the most important skills you'll need for working with electronics. Come join us for an introductory through-hole soldering workshop. Soldering enables you to create sturdy connections between electrical components. In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn how to use a soldering iron safely and effectively, and get plenty of practice with both soldering and de-soldering techniques. We'll be soldering up some Game of Life kits - LED tiles that generate nifty animations. No previous experience is required, making this introductory workshop a great choice for anyone who's curious about getting started with hardware tinkering! All materials will be provided.
OK, awesome, I want to join!

events.name: Fireside with Hans Robertson, Verkada
events.description:
South Park Commons is delighted to host Hans Robertson, Executive Chairman and Co-Founder of Verkada for a fireside chat. 

Hans Robertson is executive chairman and co-founder of Verkada, a leader in cloud-based physical security solutions. Founded in 2016 with just four employees, Hans has helped scale Verkada to more than 2,200 employees, 31,000 enterprise customers, and a valuation of $5.8 billion. Today, Hans leads Verkada’s daily operations in partnership with Verkada’s CEO, Filip Kaliszan.
Prior to Verkada, Hans co-founded another Silicon Valley Unicorn, Meraki, where he served as chief operating officer for almost a decade. During this time, he helped design the first cloud-managed enterprise networking products – including Wi-Fi, firewall, and switching systems – and led the company to a $1.2 billion acquisition with Cisco in 2012.
Prior to founding Meraki he was a product manager at EMC and was an early employee at VMware. Hans began his career as a business analyst at McKinsey & Co. Hans also serves as a Board member at Pilot and Tractian. Hans holds a bachelor’s and master’s degree in computer science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

*This event is OTR*
About South Park Commons (SPC)
SPC is a technical community and venture fund dedicated to helping founders, researchers, and technologists figure out what to work on next—what we call the -1 to 0 stage of your career. We believe this is best accomplished in the most talent-dense community possible.
SPC events are open to members, alumni, and special guests of the community. The best way to join events at SPC is to apply for SPC membership.
*Please note doors close at event start time and we are unable to accommodate pending, waitlist, or late arrivals.
